title: World heading for ‘irrevocable overshoot’ of global temperature thresholds, analysis warns
content:
Failure to cut emissions will ‘consign humanity to disasters they are unable to adapt to’, report says

The world is heading for an “irrecoverable overshoot” of global temperature thresholds that will plunge billions of people into disastrous climate impacts because governments have stalled for so long to cut planet-heating emissions, analysis has found.

Under current policies, the planet will heat up by 2.7C on average by the end of the century compared with preindustrial times, the report by Climate Action Tracker (CAT) found. This is up slightly from a prediction of 2.6C in the group’s analysis conducted last year.

title: Russia’s Leaders: Children of a Dead Age
content:
Russia is led by Vladimir Putin, Sergei Lavrov, and Valery Gerasimov, who are 74, 76, and 71 years old. When the Berlin Wall fell in 1989, heralding the end of the Soviet empire, they were already adults of 37, 39, and 34.

Their worldviews were formed in the USSR, and they still long for the days when their country oppressed Central and Eastern Europe, had influence across the globe, and was one of the world’s two superpowers.

Ukraine, in contrast, is led by much younger leaders. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is 48; Gen. Mykhailo Drapatyi, 43; and Olha Stefanishyna, the former ambassador to the US, 41. Presidential aide Kyrylo Budanov is 40, while former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov is only 35.

When the Wall came, Zelenskyy was 11, Drapatyi six, Stefanishyna four, and Budanov three. Fedorov had not yet been born. Their worldviews were developed in a free and independent Ukraine. They do not long for a return to the Soviet Union.

This age difference also explains why both sides are so adamant about winning.

title: Tunisia: Authorities must urgently investigate surge in detainees’ deaths in prisons
content:
Tunisian authorities must immediately launch prompt, impartial, and independent investigations into the alarming spike in deaths in detention during the severe heatwaves of the summer and address life-threatening prison conditions across the country to ensure this does not occur again, Amnesty International said today. 

The Tunisian League for the Defence of Human Rights (LTDH) confirmed at least 23 deaths of prisoners between July and August 2026, as Tunisia experienced its hottest summer since 1950. Extreme heat and nationwide shortages of bottled water compounded already harsh prison conditions, marked by chronic overcrowding and severe disruption to running water. Families of prisoners reported medical negligence which prison officials have denied.  

The Tunisian authorities have a duty to protect the lives and health of everyone in their custody.

Heba Morayef, Amnesty International

title: Scott Colom Wins Stunning Victory, Becomes Mississippi's First Black Senator Since Reconstruction
content:
Democrat Scott Colom has made history as Mississippi’s first Democratic senator since 1982 — and its first African American senator since the post-Civil War Reconstruction era. Colom narrowly defeated Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in a state that President Trump won by nearly 23 points in 2024. Colom’s victory brings the incoming Senate Democratic caucus to 55. Colom gave his victory speech on Wednesday at the historically Black Tougaloo College, just miles from where civil rights activist Medgar Evers was murdered in 1963 by a member of the Ku Klux Klan.

“There were times that I couldn’t get donors to answer the phone; they did not believe a moment like this was possible. But I kept the faith,” said Colom. “There are so many people that had faith in Mississippi at times where it seemed impossible, people like Medgar Evers.”

title: Indonesia: US Aid Cuts Fuel HIV
content:
(Jakarta) – United States foreign aid cuts in 2025 abruptly ended essential community-based HIV prevention and care for lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) people in Indonesia who already face discrimination and arbitrary arrest, Human Rights Watch said in a report released today. Globally, more than 170,000 additional people are estimated to have died in one year because of the cuts to HIV/AIDS response, which especially affect populations at increased risk of HIV infection.

The 33-page report, “‘We Want to Be Treated as Human’: Impact of US Foreign Aid Cuts on HIV/AIDS Prevention and Care in Indonesia,” documents the Trump administration’s dismantling of the US Agency for International Development (USAID) and finds that it eliminated services for people at greatest risk of HIV, creating additional barriers to testing, prevention, and lifesaving treatment. The Indonesian government and international donors should urgently restore support for community-led HIV/AIDS services.

title: ‘To them, we’re just NPCs’: the artists and activists challenging Trump’s video game propaganda
content:
Order a Diet Coke or invade Iran – that’s the choice facing the US president in one of several satirical games, as designers turn the gamification of politics back on the White House

In early September, the Trump White House announced a surprising new addition to its official website. Named simply Arcade, it is a collection of browser games based on classic titles such as Flappy Bird, Snake, and Tetris, but re-tuned as flagrant works of political propaganda. Designed to court reactionary gamers, they push the administration’s policies on immigration and other hot-button issues, while dehumanising their targets. There have recently been some new additions: a Temple Run clone named Red Scare about crossing the “ration market” and escaping the Democratic Socialists of America, and another simple item-matching game about the threat of socialism. In the midst of increasing fuel, utility and grocery prices thanks to the Iran war, these were naked attempts to distract voters by appealing to their video game nostalgia.

title: Poland’s Endless Battle for Justice
content:
More than a decade of conflict has deprived Poland of an accepted constitutional arbiter. Victory in the latest confrontation, whoever wins it, will not restore one. 

On October 30, Poland’s president aborted a flight to Senegal mid-route as police blockaded the Constitutional Tribunal and rival judges fought for control. By November 4, the standoff had unraveled into competing criminal allegations. Beneath the spectacle lies a fundamental crisis of authority: state institutions no longer agree on whose decisions constitute law. 

The tribunal decides whether legislation contravenes the constitution and settles disputes over constitutional powers. Its 15 judges serve non-renewable nine-year terms. Parliament’s lower house, the Sejm, elects them. The president administers their statutory oaths. That distinction matters: the constitution gives him no power to block parliament’s choice.

title: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story
content:
After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’

The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation.

Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October.

title: CODATA RDMT – Call for suggested additional terms now open; deadline 10 December 2026
content:
The CODATA Research Data Management Terminology (RDMT) https://vocabs.ardc.edu.au/viewById/685 gathers the key terms needed for a common understanding of the research data management domain. The RDMT is revised by the CODATA RDM Terminology Working Group, shared for public review, and then confirmed and finalised biennially.

The RDMT will be once again revised in 2027. In preparation for this process, we are inviting your ideas for any terms that you feel are missing from the current version (v002) of the Terminology.

Before suggesting terms, please read the RDMT scope statement, available here:

https://codata.org/initiatives/data-science-and-stewardship/rdm-terminology-wg/

Once you have verified that the term you’re interested in is a) in scope; and b) not already present within the Terminology, please add it to our suggested additions form here:

https://forms.gle/YyHGETo3FPwixPGB7

The form will close on 10 December 2026. Terms will be discussed by the 2027 RDMT Working Group.

If you are a RDM expert and interested in committing to the 2027 RDMT Working Group, please look out for the call for applications which will be advertised soon.

Valmiskursseilla pääset suoraan kouluttamaan. Tietoturvakurssimme auttavat henkilöstöä tunnistamaan arjen uhkia ja toimimaan turvallisesti. Voit aloittaa yhdestä kurssista tai rakentaa kanssamme koko verkko-oppimisen kokonaisuuden.

title: IS: Virkamiehen mukaan Ville Tavion Somalia-päätös oli lainvastainen
content:
Ulkoministeriön virkamies sanoi keskiviikkona Ilta-Sanomille, että ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavion (ps.) päätös järjestöjen Somalia-avustusten hylkäämisestä on lainvastainen.

Ministeriön kehityspoliittisen osaston päällikkö Juha Savolainen sanoi lehdelle, että Tavio ei kohdellut neljää Somalia-hanketta hallintolain edellyttämällä tavalla tasapuolisesti.

- Meillä ei ole muuta mahdollisuutta virkakuntana kuin jättää eriävä mielipide päätöksestä, Savolainen sanoi IS:lle.

Eriävän mielipiteen aikoo jättää ministeriön kansalaisyhteiskuntayksikön päällikkö Tanja Grén, joka on Savolaisen alainen ja päätöksen esittelijä.

TAVIO kertoi maanantaina Facebookissa päättäneensä olla myöntämättä rahoitusta seitsemälle Somaliaan suunnitellulle kansalaisjärjestöjen hankkeelle.

Tavio kutsui ratkaisuaan säästötoimeksi. Hänen mukaansa kehitysyhteistyö Somaliaan on keskeytetty, koska maa ei ole tehnyt riittävästi palautusyhteistyötä.

Tavion erityisavustaja Tuomas Tähti kertoi aiemmin IS:lle, että virkamiehet olivat esittäneet avustuksen myöntämistä neljälle hankkeelle, joille olisi myönnetty yhteensä 2,2 miljoonaa euroa.

title: Starlink Mobile is another Musk power grab
content:
In October, Elon Musk’s Starlink was back in the news. Ukraine’s access to the satellite communications network had once again been curtailed, following a previous restriction in 2022. Questions swirled about who was behind it: Musk himself, or the US government under Donald Trump.

There are in fact two Starlink services on offer to countries like Ukraine. There’s the commercial version we know by that name, but there’s also Starshield, the defense-oriented one that the US government has a lot more control over. Musk admitted he did limit Ukraine’s access to Starlink, but Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also suggested the US government was behind the restrictions placed on its access to Starshield. Once the service was restored, the truth of that claim was left unresolved.

The incident revived an unresolved issue from the original shutdown four years earlier: how was it that one man could wield so much power over the communications infrastructure of sovereign countries, not to mention that so many people depend on? At the time, it seemed clear that something was going to have to be done about it, but then the urgency behind that effort seemed to wane.

title: Europe's invaders have red claws
content: Lake Milada, one of Czechia's largest lakes, is home to a diverse range of animals: European catfish, greylag geese, and smooth snakes. But in September, recreational cyclists came across an unusual sight: a red crayfish marching on the path. While crayfish are not new to the country – signal and spiny-cheek crayfish have displaced native species over the years – this one was different. It was a red swamp crayfish, which is found in freshwater in about 20 European countries, but had never been spotted in Czechia before. Originally from North America, these crayfish are among the most invasive in Europe. For nature conservationist Lenka Čolobentičová and her colleagues at the country's Nature Conservation Agency, it was not good news. “They’re very aggressive; they fight a lot with other crayfish species, they carry the crayfish plague, and they reproduce quickly,” she told The European Correspondent. Though not confirmed, the agency believes it was likely released into Lake Milada by a hobbyist. Across Europe, invasive species are one of the five major causes of biodiversity loss. title: Tavion toimintatapa hanketukipäätöksessä ei ole hyvää hallintoa – perustelemme näkemyksemme
content:
Hyvän hallinnon periaatteiden mukaista olisi ollut ilmoittaa jo hakuvaiheessa linjauksesta, jonka mukaan hanketukea ei myönnetä Somaliaan. Järjestöt olisivat olleet päätöksestä erimielisiä, mutta hakuprosessi olisi ollut yhdenvertainen.

Jaa

Pääministeri Petteri Orpo (kok.) linjasi tiistaina, että ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavion (ps.) päätös hanketuen epäämisestä Somaliassa toimivilta järjestöjen hankkeilta kuuluu ministerin toimivaltaan.

Fingo ei kiistä tätä. Tämä ei kuitenkaan poista sitä, että ministerin päätöksentekotapa ei ole ollut hyvän hallinnon mukaista. Perustelemme kantamme seuraavasti:

Orpon hallitus on ohjelmassaan linjannut, että kehitysyhteistyö ehdollistetaan omien kansalaisten vastaanottamiselle. Kirjauksen perusteella Suomi keskeytti Somalian maaohjelman kaksi vuotta sitten, mutta linjasi samalla, ettei keskeytys koske kansalaisjärjestöjä, humanitaarista apua tai yksityisen sektorin tukea.

Päätös oli perusteltu: kansalaisjärjestöt eivät tee päätöksiä kotimaidensa päättäjien puolesta. Tämän linjauksen myötä ulkoministeriö myönsi esimerkiksi vuosi sitten ohjelmatukea Somaliassa toteutettaville järjestöjen ja niiden kumppaneiden ohjelmille.

title: Justice is the infrastructure the world keeps forgetting
content:
The world cannot build prosperous economies, peaceful societies or resilient democracies while neglecting its people’s everyday justice needs.

Originally published on Global Voices

Image courtesy HiiL

This post by Jude Udo Ilo is part of Global Voices’ November 2026 Spotlight series, “Justice as infrastructure.” In this Spotlight, Global Voices is partnering with The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law (HiiL) to highlight the ways justice functions as critical infrastructure for any society. You can support this coverage by donating here.

Imagine visiting a hospital with a serious illness, only to discover that every patient receives the same medication, regardless of their symptoms. We would rightly call this a failure of healthcare. Yet this is remarkably close to how justice is delivered in much of the world.

We have built justice systems around institutions rather than people, procedures rather than problems, and legal traditions rather than lived realities. We measure progress by the number of courts constructed, judges appointed and laws enacted, while paying insufficient attention to whether ordinary people can actually resolve the disputes disrupting their lives.

title: Russia Courts Africa but Investment Lags Behind Diplomacy
content:
Moscow has widened its political reach, but African governments want investment that creates jobs and reduces dependence as well as grain supplies and security agreements

By Kester Kenn Klomegah*

MOSCOW | 11 November 2026 (IDN) — African delegations came to Moscow for Russia’s third summit with the continent despite Western efforts to isolate the Kremlin. Their presence gave President Vladimir Putin a diplomatic success. The harder question is what African countries will receive from the agreements signed there: financing for factories, dependable electricity and jobs, or another round of promises.

The meeting on 28–29 October produced a cooperation programme for the next three years. But Russia’s political reach still exceeds its commercial presence. African governments can accept Russian offers while continuing to trade, borrow a|nd negotiate with Moscow’s competitors.

Moscow has widened its political reach, but African governments want investment that creates jobs and reduces dependence as well as grain supplies and security agreements

title: Sivistystyössä ansioituneita palkittiin 50-vuotisjuhlassa
content:
Kansalaisfoorumin 50-vuotisjuhlavuosi huipentui lokakuisiin juhliin. Juhlien puheissa palattiin historiaan, tähyiltiin kohti parempaa tulevaa ja kuultiin runo sivistyksestä.

Palkitut yhteisöt ja pedagogit ovat toiminnallaan tehneet selväksi, että sivistys kuuluu kaikille, se tunnistaa taiteen ja kulttuurin suuren muutosvoiman, edistää yhdenvertaisuutta ja on kestävää ja yhteisöllistä!

title: Kulttuuriympäristöpäivien kahvipaussi: Kätketyt aarteet
content:
Tervetuloa ilmoittautumaan Euroopan kulttuuriympäristöpäivien Teams-kahvipaussille. Kahvipaussin teemana on vuoden 2027 teema Kätketyt aarteet. Esittely kestää puolisen tuntia, jonka jälkeen on aikaa kysymyksille ja keskustelulle klo 16 saakka.

Euroopan kulttuuriympäristöpäivien teema vuonna 2027 on Kätketyt aarteet. Teemavuosi kutsuu katsomaan ympärillemme uusin silmin ja pysähtymään sellaisten paikkojen, perinteiden ja ilmiöiden äärelle, jotka ovat jääneet piiloon, syrjään tai huomaamatta. Millaisia tarinoita tuttujen katujen, viheralueiden, rakennusten ja yhteisöjen taakse, alle tai reunoille kätkeytyy?

Kätketyt aarteet -teema innostaa löytöretkelle kohti kulttuuriperinnön vähemmän tunnettuja helmiä ja yllättäviä kerroksia. Teemavuonna jokainen voi olla löytäjä, kertoja ja mukaan kutsuja.

Vuonna 2027 kulttuuriympäristöpäivillä voidaan avata ovia paikkoihin, joihin ei normaalisti ole pääsyä, ja paljastaa yksityiskohtia, jotka arjessa jäävät huomaamatta. Kätketyt aarteet voivat löytyä ullakoilta ja kellareista, sisäpihoilta ja takapihoilta, arkistojen kätköistä tai maisemista, joiden ohi kuljemme päivittäin pysähtymättä.

title: Metsäkatoa aiheuttava puuhiili on Tansaniassa monelle käytännöllisin energianlähde – Nyt etsitään parempia vaihtoehtoja
content:
Tuli roihuaa jo yhdellä Efrahimi Kajan pikaruokakojun liesistä. Toinen liesi on vasta syttymässä, mutta kunhan se syttyy, se kyllä palaa voimakkaasti, Kaja lupaa.

Hän käyttää ruuanlaiton polttoaineena paikallisen Ecopower-firman myymiä brikettejä perinteisemmän polttoaineen, puuhiilen, sijasta.

”Ne palavat pidempään, eli keskeytyksiä polttoaineen lisäämisen takia on vähemmän”, hän kertoo.

Kaja pyörittää bisnestään Kunduchin alueella Dar es Salaamissa. Puhelin soi, kun asiakkaat soittelevat tilauksiaan. Pannulla paistuu perunasuikaileita, ja kaksi apulaista kuorii kojun takana lisää seuraavaa erää varten.

Chips mayai on suosittu katuruoka, joka yhdistää ranskanperunat ja munakkaan. Lisäksi Kaja myy paistettuja jauhobanaaneita, naudanlihavartaita ja kanaa.

Kajan aiemmin käyttämä puuhiili on Tansaniassa etenkin kaupunkialueilla kotitalouksille keskeinen polttoaine, jota valmistetaan polttamalla puuta korkeassa, hapettomassa lämpötilassa. Siitä syntyy hiiltä muistuttavia paloja, joita käytetään muun muassa ruuanlaitossa. Puuhiili on haitallista sekä terveyden, ympäristön, että ilmaston kannalta, ja siksi sille kaivataan vaihtoehtoja.

title: Open Source AI Salons and What’s Next
content:
Dear OSI community,

The fall conference season in the US is especially busy. I’ve been fortunate enough to attend several events in the last month, but it was especially great to reconnect with the community at All Things Open. This was my first big Open Source conference as Executive Director as we hosted the State of the Source track. Many of our sessions were standing room only, and the feedback we heard was generous and useful. We’re grateful for that, and we’ll be posting recordings of the sessions soon.

The day after All Things Open, we hosted our first Open Source AI Salon. This was an important moment for us as we re-engage the community to discuss the Open Source AI Definition, look at everything we’ve collectively learned since version 1.0 was published two years ago, and chart the course for our next steps. We’ll be hosting many more of these events in the coming months. Watch this space for details.

title: Globaali turvallisuusaloite – kiinalaistyyppinen visio maailmanrauhasta vai venäläisen etupiiriajattelun siunaus?
content:
Vuonna 2022 lanseerattu julistus hahmottelee kiinalaisittain ideaalin kansainvälisen järjestyksen ydinperiaatteita.

Ukrainan sodan syttyminen helmikuussa 2022 osoitti vallitsevan kansainvälisen järjestyksen ajautuneen syvään institutionaaliseen ja normatiiviseen kriisiin. Pian sodan syttymisen jälkeen Kiina kiiruhti esittelemään visionsa kansainvälisestä turvallisuusarkkitehtuurista, jolla voitaisiin saavuttaa pysyvä rauha: globaali turvallisuusaloite (Global Security Initiative) on osa presidentti Xi Jinpingin suorastaan kantilaista visiota kansainvälisen järjestyksen uudistamisesta ”ihmiskunnan kohtalonyhteisöksi”, jossa nykypäivän anarkinen suurvaltakilpailu korvattaisiin harmoniseen rinnakkaiseloon ja tiiviiseen yhteistyöhön kykenevien, mutta ideologisesti monimuotoisten valtioiden yhteisöllä.

Globaali turvallisuusaloite voidaan nähdä kohtalonyhteisön syvimpiä, esimerkiksi kovan turvallisuuden ja valtioiden välisten suhteiden perusperiaatteita määrittelevänä julistuksena.

title: Jobbportal på engelska ska göra svenska jobbmöjligheter mer synliga internationellt
content:
Sverige konkurrerar med många andra länder om kvalificerad arbetskraft. För svenska arbetsgivare inom bland annat teknik, naturvetenskap, ingenjörsvetenskap och matematik kan tillgången till rätt kompetens vara avgörande för utveckling och tillväxt. För att möta det behovet har Svenska institutet utvecklat Jobbportalen. Portalen samlar engelskspråkiga jobbannonser från Arbetsförmedlingens Platsbank där svenska inte är ett krav.

– Sverige har mycket att erbjuda internationella talanger, men intresse måste kunna omsättas i konkreta möjligheter till arbete. Den nya jobbportalen gör det enklare för internationell spetskompetens att hitta svenska arbetsgivare som söker deras kompetens. Det stärker både företagens konkurrenskraft och Sveriges förmåga att konkurrera om talang, säger Madeleine Sjöstedt, generaldirektör för Svenska institutet.

title: Spain general strike: how 50 years of industrial action shaped Spain’s post-Franco democracy
content:
The end of the Franco dictatorship profoundly changed labour relations in Spain. Under Franco, trade unions were wholly authoritarian, and there was only one permitted union, the Spanish Syndical Organisation or “Sindicato Vertical”. But after Franco’s death in 1975 and the subsequent transition to democracy, trade unions and employers’ organisations received full constitutional recognition as the main players in collective bargaining.

During the transition to democracy, which lasted from 1977 to 1982, employers and unions engaged in social dialogue with the aim of consolidating Spain’s young democracy, and to mitigate the severe economic crisis that began in 1977. The crisis stemmed from overproduction and a sharp rise in oil prices, leading to soaring production costs and high inflation and unemployment.

This social dialogue, known as concertación, ensured social peace, and brought about multiple landmark labour agreements in the early 1980s.

title: El Salvador is exporting the ‘Bukele model’ to Haiti – but the gang offensive is a gamble for both nations
content:
On Nov. 10, 2026, El Salvador President Nayib Bukele posted footage of attack helicopters firing on a compound near Haiti’s capital, Port-au-Prince.

He had earlier requested, via a social media post in Haitian Creole, the address of Wilson Joseph, leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, one of Haiti’s most powerful criminal organizations. Bukele subsequently claimed the operation, conducted with Haitian police, had demolished Joseph’s residence and gang headquarters. As many as 20 people were killed, although Joseph was reportedly absent.

The attack comes amid a flurry of anti-gang operations in Haiti. On Nov. 6, Mathias Saintil, head of the “Boston” gang in Cité Soleil, was killed in a drone strike by a Haitian special task force, prompting Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé to declare on the social media platform X “one less gang leader.” Erik Prince, founder of the private military firm Vectus Global, responded: “Nice shot.”

title: Scientists Discovered An ‘Invisible’ Object In Space. It’s Challenging Our Understanding of the Cosmos
content:
Scientists have discovered a bizarre “invisible” object in space that challenges our understanding of stellar evolution and could help resolve longstanding astronomical mysteries, according to a study published on Wednesday in Science Advances. Its orbit and mass are so strange, in fact, that researchers ran thousands of simulations and couldn’t reproduce them. 

The hidden object is likely an ultra-rare supermassive neutron star, which is the collapsed core that is left over after a massive star goes supernova. Located in a system called J0008+0128,, the object was detected through its gravitational effects on its companion, a red giant star.

Massive stars that go supernova either collapse into neutron stars or black holes, both of which belong to a wider family of dead stars known as “stellar remnants.” But for decades, astronomers have puzzled over the so-called “mass gap" between neutron stars and black holes, which is the observed scarcity of remnants between 2.5 and five times as massive as the Sun.

title: From Maricarmen’s eviction to the general strike: how Spain’s youth are defying the housing crisis
content:
Almost two months after the eviction of Maricarmen, the 87-year-old woman whose subsequent death sparked a movement, Spain’s housing encampments demanding change remain steadfast. Sofía Guerrero Orte, Alberto Pérez Madrona and Pablo Rodríguez Rodríguez, three university students involved in Seville’s encampment since the beginning, explain how the movement has grown and triggered an election, becoming the driving force behind Spain’s first general strike in 14 years.

“These young people today… they don’t protest like they used to…” They call us the “generación de cristal” or the “Glass Generation”.  They say we are fragile, but here we are protesting and resilient – because when glass breaks it cuts.

To many on the outside it may have looked like the Spanish housing protests happened overnight – an outpouring of grief and rage following Maricarmen’s eviction in September. But the lack of affordable housing has long suffocated students, young people, elderly people, single mums and marginalized populations, such as racialized groups – those of us who are already at higher risk of social exclusion.

title: Analysis: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as countries meet at COP31
content:
The amount of public funding pledged to help developing countries tackle climate change has dropped by more than 70% in 2026, according to Carbon Brief analysis.

Developed countries are required under UN climate treaties to provide “climate finance” and have traditionally announced multi-year pledges to feed into their global commitments.

Most of these pledges expired in 2025 and, since then, the US has withdrawn from international climate efforts and many European aid budgets have been cut.

A civil-society tracker shows that only five nations have announced new multi-year pledges, including just one major donor – the UK.

Germany, France and Japan are among the key contributors that have so far failed to set out plans for new climate finance, while none is expected from the US.

As a result, the total amount of public climate finance pledged over the next few years amounts to just $11.7bn a year in spending, down from recent levels of around $40bn.

Experts tell Carbon Brief that global conflict, fiscal constraints and the rise of the far right are all making it harder for developed-country governments to pledge new funds.

title: "Birds of War": New Film Tells a Story of Love and Journalism from Syria to Lebanon
content:
We speak with Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak, filmmakers and subjects of the new documentary Birds of War, which tells their epic love story through years of upheaval in the Middle East. Boulos, a London-based Lebanese journalist working for the BBC, and Habak, a Syrian activist and cameraman, first connected while covering the Syrian civil war and stayed in touch through years of war, revolution and exile, forming a relationship that is chronicled in the documentary by drawing on 13 years of their personal videos, voice notes and other correspondence.

The film also examines the unequal relationship between international news organizations and local journalists whose work they rely on, the fraught political history between Syria and Lebanon, and how Boulos and Habak’s personal connection overcame those divisions.

“Without our journalistic relationship, [we] would have never been together. I would have never opened my heart to somebody like him,” says Boulos. “We can be any race, any gender, any religion, any background, but at the same time we’re all humans.”

title: 🤕 Medicare's AI Experiment | EFFector 38.20
content:
When we need medical care, we expect decisions about our treatment to be made by our doctors, not a tech company's algorithm. But in January, the federal government launched a program that uses AI to evaluate Medicare beneficiaries' requests for certain procedures.

EFF sued for records on WISeR, seeking badly needed transparency about Medicare's AI experiment. In our latest EFFector newsletter, we're talking about what happens when the government outsources treatment approval to private AI companies—without sufficient transparency, testing, or legal limits.

JOIN OUR NEWSLETTER

For over 35 years, EFFector has been your guide to understanding the intersection of technology, civil liberties, and the law. This issue covers unconstitutional digital dragnets, a post office surveillance scheme, and what EFF uncovered about Medicare's AI experiment.

Prefer to listen in? EFFector is now available on all major podcast platforms. This time we're talking to EFF's Lena Cohen about WISeR records documenting improper denials, operational chaos, and lengthy delays that have left patients waiting in pain. title: Case of Death Row Prisoner Peyman Farah-Avar Referred to Sentence Enforcement Branch
content:
According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, Peyman Farah-Avar’s case has been referred to the Sentence Enforcement Branch.

An informed source close to the political prisoner’s family told HRANA: “On Monday, November 9, Mr. Farah-Avar informed his family during a phone call that he had received an official notification indicating that his case had been referred to the Sentence Enforcement Branch.”

Mr. Farah-Avar’s request for retrial, which had been registered with a branch of the Supreme Court, was rejected by the judicial authority on April 26, 2026. His death sentence had previously been upheld by Branch 39 of the Supreme Court in September of 2025.

Mr. Farah-Avar had earlier been sentenced to death on charges of “baghi” (armed rebellion) and “moharebeh” (enmity against God) by Branch 1 of the Rasht Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Ahmad Darvish Goftar.

An informed source close to the political prisoner’s family had previously confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “These charges were brought against Mr. Farah-Avar based on his poetry and protest activities concerning social justice and civil rights.”

title: Etla nostaa teollisuuden kasvuennustettaan − työllisyysnykäystä saadaan kuitenkin vielä odottaa
content:
Suomen teollisuus kasvaa tänä vuonna kaksi ja puoli prosenttia, arvioi Elinkeinoelämän tutkimuslaitos toimialakohtaisessa ennusteessaan. Etla on nostanut ennustettaan keväästä yli puoli prosenttiyksikköä. Myös palvelualoille on luvassa aiemmin ennakoitua vahvempia kasvunäkymiä. Voimakkainta kasvua on luvassa metalliteollisuuteen ja informaatio- ja viestintäalalle, jossa tekoälyn mahdollisuudet vahvistavat tuottavuuskehitystä. Teollisuuden työllisyysnykäystä ylöspäin saadaan kuitenkin odottaa vielä ensi vuoteen. Yhdysvaltojen välivaalien tulos ei välttämättä tarkoita muutoksia tullipolitiikkaan, vaikka välit EU:hun näyttävät nyt seesteisemmiltä.

Etlan syksyn Suhdanne-ennusteessa Suomen talouden kasvuksi ennustettiin tänä vuonna 1,7 prosenttia. Ensi vuodelle kasvun ennakoidaan kiihtyvän 1,9 prosenttiin ja vaimenevan sitten 1,4 prosenttiin vuonna 2028. Ennustevuosina talouskasvu on yritysvetoista eli se tulee suurelta osin yksityiseltä sektorilta.

title: The AI x Journalism Summit returns to Baltimore May 5-6, plus AI Real Talk on Nov. 12
content:
Our third annual AI x Journalism Summit is May 5-6, 2027 in Baltimore, and tickets are on sale now! Early bird pricing is $99 through Nov. 30.

Two new tracks join Adopt and Govern in 2027: Sustain, on revenue, licensing, audience, costs and staffing, and Frontier, on technologies that haven't reached newsrooms yet. We're also adding two session formats: Masterclasses that go deep on one topic or skill, and debates that put two or more sides of an unsettled question on stage.

Session pitches are also open. We're looking for sessions that give people something practical they can use, teach them something new or start a conversation they didn't expect.

Gina Chua and Adiel Kaplan of the Tow-Knight Center for Journalism Futures join our latest AI Real Talk on Thursday, Nov. 12, at noon ET (17:00 UTC). They'll talk about their report, The Three-Layer Cake, which argues that the most useful work for journalism now sits in shared infrastructure, not inside individual newsrooms.

“Human attention is finite; intention is not.”
Gina Chua and Adiel Kaplan, The Three-Layer Cake

title: Helsingin yliopiston johtamalle konsortiolle 10 miljoonan euron ERC Synergy-rahoitus ihmisen perimän salaisuuksien tutkimiseen
content:
An international consortium led by Professor Sakari Vanharanta and Professor Lauri Aaltonen from the University of Helsinki (Finland), Professor Jussi Taipale from the Wellcome Sanger Institute (UK) and Professor Carl de Boer from the University of British Columbia (Canada) has been awarded a prestigious European Research Council (ERC) Synergy Grant for the project FIBERMAP. The consortium receives a total of around €10 million, of which around €4.5 million goes to the University of Helsinki's subprojects.

The ERC Synergy Grant is among Europe’s most competitive and highly regarded research funding instruments, supporting small groups of outstanding researchers whose complementary expertise enables them to tackle the most challenging scientific questions. The FIBERMAP consortium brings together world-leading expertise in high-throughput biochemistry, human genomics, computational biology and cancer research.

title: Türkiye: COP31 Host Continues Support for Coal Expansion
content:
(Istanbul, November 11, 2026) – While world leaders gather in Antalya for the United Nations climate change conference (COP31) on November 11 and 12 to discuss how to accelerate global climate action and implement their climate commitments, Turkish authorities’ reluctance to stop expansion of coal operations in the country and plan an exit from fossil fuels sends the wrong message as the co-host of COP31 and undermines the credibility of its commitments and agenda, Human Rights Watch said today. 

In July 2026, the Turkish government appealed a June court ruling rejecting a plan to add two new units to the Afşin-Elbistan coal power plant A in Türkiye’s southeastern Kahramanmaraş province. In the same month, the government embarked on the permit process to expand the capacity of an existing coal power plant in the northwestern Çanakkale province.

title: EDUCA: Härliga, hemska finska
content:
Finska – hur kan vi öka självförtroendet och motivationen att lära sig? På Educa-mässan lanserar Svenska kulturfonden och Åbo Akademi den strategiska satsningen Finska i lag för att stödja finskundervisningen. Välkommen på ett miniseminarium där vi ser mera och mindre allvarligt på läget.   

I början av 2027 startar Kulturfondens och Åbo Akademis stora satsning på finskundervisningen i den grundläggande utbildningen och på andra stadiet. Sammanlagt satsar Kulturfonden 2,6 miljoner euro på undervisningen i finska.  

På Educa-mässan får du veta mera om utmaningar och trender, vad satsningen går ut på och hur du kan bli en del av den. 

Seminariet avrundas av skådespelaren Dennis Nylund som discodansläraren Folke Rundqvist.  

Fredag 29.1.2027 kl. 14-16, programmet slutar kl.15.30, efter det bjuder vi på eftermiddagsfika 

Helsingfors mässcentrum, Mässplatsen 1, kongressflygeln Siipi, konferensrum 208. Om du inte besöker Educa-mässan kan du använda Siipis ingång via Järnvägsmannagatan 3. 

Programmet är särskilt för alla som undervisar i finska, rektorer, bildningschefer, utbildningsadministratörer, forskare och också andra intresserade.

title: Eläinlääkäriliiton yrittäjäpalkinto Aures iho- ja korvaeläinlääkäreille
content:
Eläinlääkäriliiton yrittäjäpalkinto on myönnetty Aures eläinlääkärit Oy:n perustajille Kirsti Schildtille ja Katja Kyröläiselle. Palkinto julkistettiin Eläinlääkäripäivien avajaisissa 11. marraskuuta 2026 Helsingin Messukeskuksessa.

– Tämä on hirmuisen suuri kunnia, ja me pidämme tätä palkintoa suuressa arvossa, perustaja Kirsti Schildt sanoo.

Aures on Suomen ainoa ainoastaan kissojen ja koirien iho- ja korvasairauksiin keskittynyt pieneläinklinikka.

Eläinlääkäriliiton hallitus perustelee valintaansa yrityksen innovatiivisella liiketoiminnalla, joka nojautuu hyvään työkulttuuriin ja -ilmapiiriin. Hallitus valitsee palkinnon saajan liiton jäsenten ehdotusten pohjalta.

Kirsti Schildt ällistyi kuultuaan, että palkinto myönnetään Aurekselle. Yritys on perustettu vuonna 2021, ja perustajat kertovat ihailevansa monia aiempina vuosina palkittuja yrittäjiä.

Aures sai alkunsa perustajien yhteisestä haaveesta tuoda osaava joukko dermatologian ammattilaisia saman katon alle. Käytännössä tämä mahdollistaa sen, että esimerkiksi atooppinen koira pystytään lähettämään tutulta lähiklinikalta ihotauteihin erikoistuneiden eläinlääkärien tutkittavaksi.

title: KAMKin uusi kasvihuone hyödyntää konesalien lämpöä
content:
Ylijäämälämmöllä tarkoitetaan datakeskusten ja konesalien jäähdytyksessä syntyvää lämpöä. Kajaanissa jo toimivien sekä rakenteilla ja suunnitteilla olevien datakeskusten myötä myös sen määrä kasvaa tulevaisuudessa. Tämän vuoksi erilaiset hyödyntämisratkaisut kiinnostavat niin datakeskusalaa, yrityksiä kuin aluekehittäjiäkin.

HUKKIS-kasvihuone toimii uudenlaisena tutkimus-, kehitys- ja innovaatioympäristönä sekä oppimisympäristönä. Opiskelijoille se tarjoaa mahdollisuuden oppia käytännössä energianhallinnasta, kiertotaloudesta ja ruoantuotannosta. Yritykset saavat mahdollisuuden pilotoida uusia ratkaisuja ja testata niiden toimivuutta todellisessa käyttöympäristössä.

Kasvihuoneessa voidaan tuottaa tietoa muun muassa energiatehokkuudesta, ylijäämälämmön hyödyntämisestä sekä datakeskustoiminnan ympärille rakentuvista uusista liiketoimintamahdollisuuksista.

"Tietojemme mukaan vastaavanlaista datakeskusten ylijäämälämpöön perustuvaa kasvihuonetta opetus- ja TKI-ympäristönä ei Suomessa – eikä kai maailmallakaan – ole aiemmin toteutettu." toteaa hankkeen projektipäällikkö Silja Keränen.

title: 118 konstnärer fick mobilitetsstöd i årets sista omgång
content:
Mobilitetsstödet är till för professionella konstnärers eller kulturarbetares resor och/eller vistelse inom de nordiska och/eller baltiska länderna. Sakkunniggruppens ordförande Orri Huginn Ágústsson berättar att ansökningarna höll en hög professionell nivå. Omgången visade på en bred variation av konstnärliga discipliner och aktiviteter.

– Förutom projekt inom scenkonst, bildkonst och musik fanns det intressanta projekt inom kulturarv, foto, film och litteratur. Denna ansökningsomgång innefattade även tvärvetenskapliga projekt i samarbete med bl.a. arkitekter, säger Orri Huginn Ágústsson.

Bland de konstnärer som fick resestöd fanns barnkulturdesignern och konstnären Zala Seles som kommer resa från Sverige till Färöarna för att jobba med projektet Future Streetscapes. Projektet, som äger rum under Democracy Festival for Children, innefattar flera workshoppar där barn ges möjlighet att se på offentliga utrymmen med nya ögon genom att tillsammans utforska material, praktiskt modellbyggande och AR-teknik (augmented reality).

title: 118 artists awarded mobility funding in the final round of the year
content:
Mobility funding is available for professional artists’ or cultural practitioners’ travel and/or stay within the Nordic and/or Baltic countries. Orri Huginn Ágústsson, chair of the expert group, says that the applications were of a high professional standard. The round featured a wide range of artistic disciplines and activities.

“Alongside projects in the performing arts, visual arts, and music, there were interesting projects in cultural heritage, photography, film, and literature. This application round also included interdisciplinary projects involving collaborations with architects, among others,” says Orri.

Among the recipients of mobility funding was children’s culture designer and artist Zala Seles, who will travel from Sweden to the Faroe Islands to work on the Future Streetscapes project. Taking place during the Democracy Festival for Children, the project involves a series of workshops that encourage children to see public spaces in a new light through the collaborative exploration of materials, hands-on model-making, and augmented reality (AR) technology.

title: Bosnian Raids Smash Two Crime Rings, Net 15 Arrests
content:
Bosnian authorities arrested 15 people in a sweeping multi-agency operation aimed at dismantling two organized crime groups suspected of drug trafficking and money laundering, the Zenica-Doboj Canton Ministry of Interior announced Wednesday. Thirteen suspects were detained in the Zenica-Doboj Canton and two in Sarajevo with all scheduled to be transferred to the Federal Police Administration for further questioning.

The raids resulted in the seizure of more than 100,000 convertible marks ($56,735) in cash, nine cars, a motorcycle, weapons, and drug-weighing equipment, according to the statement. The ministry noted that ongoing law enforcement activities related to the case have so far led to the seizure of about 150 kilograms of narcotics and 83 liters of oil used for amphetamine production.

The Federal Prosecutor's Office, which supervised the crackdown alongside the Supreme Court, stated that the broader operational activities targeted "dozens of individuals" to gather evidence documenting the syndicates' crimes. Searches were executed across four cantons, as well as in Republika Srpska, in coordination with the state intelligence agency and federal police.

title: Watch Seoul’s 6,500-Year Evolution in a Mesmerizing 3D Animated Time Lapse
content: In this century, few countries have been as visibly successful as South Korea. China’s vertiginous economic rise once absorbed vast amounts of news-media attention, but its soft power has comparatively little reach across the wider world, at least in English-speaking countries. By this point, many if not most Westerners haven’t just eaten Korean food, but also driven a Korean car, heard Korean pop music, or watched a Korean film or TV show. The resulting sense of familiarity can prove deceptive to those who eventually make the trip there, but it does, at least, mark an improvement on the scant knowledge of the place they had before. Not so long ago, they could say little with certainty except this: South Korea’s got Seoul.

title: Ahead of Spanish election, Sánchez takes aim at TikTok
content:
MADRID — Trailing in the polls ahead of Nov. 29 national elections, Spain’s ruling Socialist Party is turning to TikTok. Not to use it, but to try to ban it. 

Following the publication on Monday of a Spanish investigation accusing TikTok of allowing child sexual abuse material, the youth ministry announced it would try to block the platform.

On Wednesday the prosecutor’s office opened a preliminary inquiry, prompting a triumphant post on X by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. “Great news,” he wrote. “The days of impunity on social media are over. No platform is above the law, and much less above the rights of our children.”

The bombshell report by civil society group Maldita has shocked Spain and given the government a chance to show it’s tough on Big Tech just ahead of a momentous election, with polls showing the right firmly ahead.

Over the past 72 hours the government has pulled every available legal lever against TikTok, including lodging cases with both the Data Protection Agency and the public prosecutor’s office.

title: Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubbin puheenvuoro valtionjohtajien kokouksessa YK:n ilmastokokouksessa (COP31) Antalyassa, Turkissa, 11. marraskuuta 2026
content:
Puheen alkuperäinen kieli on englanti

Muutosvarauksin

Arvoisa presidentti,
arvoisat valtionjohtajat,
hyvät naiset ja herrat

Haluan kiittää Turkkia ja presidentti Erdoğania tämän kokouksen järjestämisestä täällä Antalyassa.

Kansainvälisen politiikan asialista ei läheskään aina täysin vastaa maailmaan todellisia haasteita. Ilmastonmuutos vaikuttaa meihin kaikkiin, mutta se jää jatkuvasti liian vähälle huomiolle. Siksi tämä kokous on entistäkin tärkeämpi. Meidän on keskityttävä siihen, mikä on tärkeintä: yhteiseen tulevaisuuteemme.

Nykyinen 1,5 asteen tavoite on vaakalaudalla. Näemme seuraukset jo nyt eri puolilla maailmaa: tuhoisina tulvina Nepalissa, merenpinnan nousuna rannikkoalueilla ja pienissä saarivaltioissa sekä maastopaloina Euroopassa. Yksikään maa – sen koosta, vaikutusvallasta tai maantieteellisestä sijainnista riippumatta – ei voi suojautua ilmastonmuutoksen seurauksilta. Eikä kukaan meistä voi ratkaista tilannetta yksin.

Haluan nostaa esiin kolme painopistettä, jotka ovat ratkaisevia COP31-kokouksen onnistumiselle.

Ensinnäkin ilmastokriisiä ei voida ratkaista ilman monenkeskisyyttä.

title: A Tool Built by Election Deniers Said These Voters Were Dead. We Found Them Alive.
content:
Ahead of the midterms, conservative election activists discussed plans to wield a powerful new weapon in the war against fraud: a data tool built by one of their own that could identify suspicious voters and help with contesting their ballots.

The system was put to the test this week in Forsyth County, Georgia, where a member of the county’s election board provided other officials with what he suggested was evidence of wrongdoing: four allegedly dead voters.

But it turns out all four are alive and well, ProPublica determined. The board rejected the attempt to challenge their ballots.

The effort, though, shows that even after last week’s blue wave, those who believe the 2020 election was stolen have continued to relentlessly search for ways to contest Republican losses. In Georgia, Democrats swept statewide offices.

title: Det finlandssvenska temanumret av Vi Läser ute nu
content:
Litteraturmagasinet Vi Läser har utkommit med ett nytt och fullspäckat specialnummer om den svenska litteraturen i Finland i samarbete med SLS.

Läs om hur Anders Mård, Anna-Lena Laurén och René Nyberg ser på sitt tidigare hemland Ryssland och hur de idag förhåller sig till det ryska folket och litteraturen. Det handlar om en komplicerad relation.

Möt Pekka Strang, snart aktuell i tv-serien The White Lotus, som berättar om sin bokhylla.

Philip Teirs författarporträtt av Tua Forsström lyfter hennes relation till litteraturen, den egna och andras. Hon ser sig som en återvändare och en omläsare.

Det finlandssvenska specialnumret distribueras till tidningens prenumeranter i samband med att året sista nummer utkommer. Det kan också läsas gratis här.

Tidningen ges ut med stöd av SLS, Svenska kulturfonden, Amos Andersons fond och Stiftelsen Brita Maria Renlunds minne.

Artikkeli Det finlandssvenska temanumret av Vi Läser ute nu julkaistiin ensimmäisen kerran SLS.

title: The 37 best Christmas gifts in the UK for tweens – chosen by 10- to 12-year-olds
content:

• The best Christmas gifts for teenagers

Buying for someone in the tweenage years can be a balancing act: while some kids are still crafting, enjoying board games and deep into Lego, others have moved on to skincare and guitars.

So, in an effort to cover the whole range, I spoke to 20 tweens (from 10 to 12 years old) from across the country. But instead of asking what they want, I quizzed them on the things they already have, truly love and use regularly. Here are their tried and tested gift ideas for a range of prices.

title: Kaakkois-Suomi: vaalipiiri Euroopan rajalla
content:
Kalle Pusa

Kaakkois-Suomen vaalipiiri ilmestyi kartalle vasta yksitoista vuotta sitten, vuoden 2015 vaaleissa, kun Kymen ja Etelä-Savon vaalipiirit yhdistyivät. Vaalipiiri ulottuu Pyhtään rannoilta Pieksämäen Vedenjakajalle. Siihen kuuluu vanhoja teollisuuskaupunkeja, kuten Kouvola, Lappeenranta ja Mikkeli, mutta myös Saimaan järvimaisemaa sekä Itämeren rantoja. Maantieteellisesti sirpaleisesta vaalipiiristä valitaan 15 kansanedustajaa.

Vihreillä on ollut Kaakkois-Suomesta parhaimmillaan kaksi kansanedustajaa. Istuva kansanedustaja Hanna Holopainen valittiin jatkokaudelle vuoden 2023 vaaleissa. Holopainen ei ole vielä ilmoittanut virallisesti päätöksestään asettua tai olla asettumatta ehdolle ensi keväänä. 

Vaalipiiri jakaa pitkän maarajan Venäjän kanssa. Siellä sijaitsee Vaalimaan, Nuijamaan ja Imatran raja-asema sekä Vainikkalan kansainvälinen rautatieraja-asema. Aikanaan osa vaalipiirin asukkaista äänestikin Viipurin läntisessä vaalipiirissä.

Kun Hanna-Kaisa Lähde oli 10-vuotias, hänen kotikylässään Joutsenossa perustettiin nykyisen vaalipiirin vanhin vihreiden paikallisyhdistys. 

Siitä on nyt yli neljäkymmentä vuotta.

title: WITNESS calls for stronger AI transparency rules and privacy protections in the US
content:
As AI-generated and manipulated content becomes increasingly common online, knowing where digital content comes from and how it has been changed is becoming more important. But efforts to improve transparency must also protect people’s privacy and security. This is especially important for activists, journalists, and human rights defenders, whose work documenting and exposing human rights violations can put them at risk.

WITNESS has been working with policymakers in the United States to advance legislation that helps people assess the origin and authenticity of digital content while safeguarding human rights. In California and New York, the organization has focused on strengthening rules around content provenance, AI disclosures, and personal data protection.

California: Strengthening transparency and content provenance

California has become a key center for AI regulation in the United States. WITNESS engages  with lawmakers on proposals addressing AI transparency and content provenance, a form of ‘watermark’ showing where digital content comes from, how it was created, and whether it has been changed.

content:
Ukrainan sota on saamassa yhä karumpia ja julmempia piirteitä. Venäjän harjoittama siviili- ja infrastruktuurikohteiden pommitus näyttää osoittautuvan varsin tehokkaaksi, pommittajan kannalta. Vaikutus ei ole suoraan sotilaallinen, vaan ilmenee yhteiskunnan kestävyyden riskinä.  Jos sitä jatkuu vuosikausia – ja Venäjällä on periaatteessa voimavaroja niin tehdä – tulee Kiova muistuttamaan toisen maailmansodan jälkeisiä rauniokaupunkeja. Onko tämän estäminen mahdotonta?

Käsittääkseni ei ole, mutta se edellyttää kahdentasoisia toimia Euroopalta. Aivan ensimmäiseksi Euroopan tulee välittömästi antaa Ukrainalle aseita sekä puolustukseen että hyökkäykseen. Nyt on keskityttävä seuraavaan vuoteen, erityisesti talveen. Toisaalta on otettava aktiivinen rooli neuvotteluissa pysyvän rauhan aikaansaamiseksi.

title: Orpo myöntää ”uuden lisämutkan”
content:
Pääministeri Petteri Orpon (kok.) mukaan Suomi tukee vahvasti Saksan liittokanslerin Friedrich Merzin näkemystä siitä, että EU:n vuosien 2028-34 budjetista ei voida sopia ennen kuin Ukrainan tukemisesta on päästy EU:ssa sopuun.

Merzin linjaus on herättänyt kritiikkiä muun muassa Slovakiassa, jonka kansallismielinen pääministeri Robert Fico kutsui tiistaina Merzin näkemystä kiristykseksi, jollaiseen Slovakia ei alistu.

Myös Tshekin pääministeri Andrej Babis suhtautui tiistaina varauksellisesti Merzin näkemyksiin.

Epävirallisessa huippukokouksessa ei tehdä asiasta päätöksiä, mutta neuvotteluja on määrä jatkaa Brysselissä kahden viikon päästä järjestettävässä varsinaisessa huippukokouksessa.

title: The EU wants to make the internet less shitty
content: “It needs to be nice at first. But then make it shitty,” says the “enshittificator” in a Norwegian Consumer Council video, who explains how companies offering digital services have made the internet less user-friendly. It's satire of “enshittification”, a concept coined by author Cory Doctorow to describe how much of the internet has got less useful or even worse over the years. It taps into growing frustration with online services that use “dark patterns” to nudge people to buy things they may not want, along with addictive design to keep us scrolling. Think of prices you can't find on a website, subscriptions that are incredibly hard to cancel, or warnings that a product is running out so you need to buy it now. Can we clean this up? The European Commission thinks it can, by cracking down on some of these manipulative features. It wants to ban dark patterns and require companies to tell us how to switch off addictive features that encourage compulsive or excessive use. The Digital Fairness Act, to be unveiled today, promises a new world of online shopping with “clearer, more neutral choices, easier-to-understand pricing and fewer frictions when joining, using or leaving digital

title: Restoring social media access comes at a cost in Gabon
content:
Citizens in Gabon went 248 days without access to Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube

Originally published on Global Voices

Image of a smartphone showing the Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, YouTube, and Messenger apps. Screenshot from the DW Afrique YouTube channel.

After more than eight months of government blockage, Gabon has restored its social media access. But it has come at a cost. This reinstatement comes with a tighter regulatory framework and an unprecedented cooperation between the government and various tech giants, raising serious concerns about freedom of expression and privacy.

On February 17, 2026, Gabon’s media regulator, the High Communication Authority (HAC), suspended major social media networks, including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, “until further notice.” According to the regulator, quoted in the daily newspaper L’Essentiel, this measure targeted not only content “undermining national security” but also content involving defamation, cyberbullying, hate speech, and threats to social cohesion.

title: Beyond Endless Struggle: What The Battle of Algiers Still Teaches Us About Revolution
content:
By Sam Ben-Meir *

NEW YORK | 11 November 2026 (IDN) —In Paul Thomas Anderson’s One Battle After Another (2025), Leonardo DiCaprio’s character, Bob Ferguson, a disillusioned former revolutionary, watches Gillo Pontecorvo’s The Battle of Algiers (1966) on television. The juxtaposition is almost comical: a man whose revolutionary aspirations have collapsed into private survival contemplates one of cinema’s most powerful representations of collective struggle. Yet the scene raises a question Anderson’s film never fully confronts: What distinguishes a revolution capable of transforming the world from a rebellion condemned to repeat itself?

The juxtaposition is especially timely. On November 7, The Battle of Algiers was screened at the Brooklyn Academy of Music as part of Playback: The Brooklyn Watch Party, selected by actor John Turturro. Sixty years after its release, Pontecorvo’s film remains a challenge to the diminished revolutionary imagination of our time, insisting that resistance need not become perpetual repetition: even seemingly immovable structures of domination can be transformed.

title: Cabo Verde’s presidential election: the stakes in one of Africa’s most stable democracies
content:
Cape Verde’s presidential election takes place against the backdrop of a democratic record that remains unusual in its regional context. The country, made up of an archipelago of islands off the coast of west Africa, has sustained multiparty competition for more than three decades. It has had peaceful transfers of power and no coups or military takeovers since independence from Portugal in 1975.

Cabo Verde (population 530,000) is a semi-presidential republic in which the president is directly elected. The prime minister is appointed by the president in light of parliamentary election results, and heads a government that is politically accountable to the national assembly.

The president represents the state and safeguards the constitution, while the prime minister and the government conduct public policy.

The presidency nevertheless carries substantial political weight. The president can veto legislation, request constitutional review and, under certain conditions, dissolve parliament. The office also entails responsibilities in foreign affairs and national defence.

title: Meet David Morales: Providence Voters Elect Democratic Socialist Mayor, Approve Israel Divestment
content:
Voters in Providence, Rhode Island, approved a ballot measure last week that could result in the city divesting from Israel. The successful grassroots campaign makes Providence the first U.S. city to pass a binding divestment measure through a popular vote. The measure instructs the city to divest from countries and companies implicated in “ethnic cleansing, apartheid, illegal military occupation, or genocide.” The language does not mention Israel by name. We speak with one of the key backers of the divestment measure, Mayor-elect David Morales, a 28-year-old democratic socialist who made history on election night as the youngest mayor ever elected in Providence.

“What we saw was our neighbors coming out in the thousands to demonstrate that we are ready for change,” Morales says, promising to enact his affordability-focused platform. “It’s the responsibility of local government to take action. And for that reason, we are seeing a rise in democratic socialism and the representation of democratic socialists all across the country.”

title: Five Individuals Arrested by Security Forces Across Three Provinces
content:
According to HRANA, citing Mizan News Agency, the Kermanshah Province Intelligence Department announced that five individuals had been identified and arrested across several provinces in Iran.

In its statement, the Kermanshah Province Intelligence Department claimed that the five individuals were affiliated with separatist groups and had connections with Israeli and U.S. intelligence services. According to the statement, they were identified and arrested in Tehran, Alborz, and Kermanshah provinces.

The statement further alleged that these individuals had also “played a significant role in damaging public property and spreading fear and intimidation in their respective provinces” during the protests of January 2026.

The report provides no further details regarding the detainees’ full identities, their places of detention, the evidence supporting the allegations against them, or the status of the judicial proceedings in their cases.

title: Kysely: Suomalaiset suhtautuvat kriittisesti asekauppaan Israelin kanssa
content:
Suomalaisista 46 prosenttia on täysin tai jokseenkin samaa mieltä siitä, että seuraavan hallituksen tulee lopettaa asekauppa Israelin kanssa, osoittaa IRO Researchin Amnestylle toteuttama kysely (liiteenä). Eri mieltä väittämästä on 39 prosenttia. Suomalaisten enemmistö ei näin ollen tue nykyisen linjan jatkamista.

Lokakuussa 2026 toteutetussa kyselyssä tuhannelta vastaajalta kysyttiin myös, onko hyväksyttävää, että Suomi ostaa aseita Israelista. 49 prosenttia ei pidä aseostoja hyväksyttävinä, kun taas 39 prosenttia hyväksyy ne.

”Suomalaisten näkemykset jakautuvat, mutta kysely osoittaa, ettei asekaupan jatkaminen Israelin kanssa nauti selvää kansalaisten tukea. On siis perusteltua edelleen keskustella siitä, millaista vastuuta Suomi kantaa hankkiessaan aseita valtiolta, jonka toimet Gazassa täyttävät kansanmurhan tunnusmerkit”, sanoo Amnestyn Suomen osaston toiminnanjohtaja Frank Johansson.

title: Suhdanne Toimialat Syksy 2026
content:
Toimialat-julkaisu sisältää yksityiskohtaista tietoa eri toimialoilta. Se kattaa metalliteollisuuden, metsäteollisuuden, kemian- ja elintarviketeollisuuden, rakentamisen sekä suurimman osan yksityisestä palvelusektorista. Toimialaennusteet on tehty Etlan syyskuussa julkaistun Suhdanne Syksy 2026 -makrotalouden ennusteen pohjalta käyttämällä mm. Suomen kansantalouden panos-tuotosmallia.

Ennusteemme mukaan Suomen kansantalous kasvaa tänä vuonna 1,7 prosenttia. Kasvu kiihtyy ensi vuonna 1,9 prosenttiin, mutta vaimenee sitten 1,4 prosenttiin vuodeksi 2028. Ennustevuosina talouskasvu on yritysvetoista, eli se tulee suurelta osin yksityiseltä sektorilta. Sekä jalostus että palvelut kasvavat nyt, mutta toistaiseksi työmarkkinatilanne ei ole kohentunut jalostuksessa. Yksityisissä palveluissa (pl. kaupanala sekä informaatio ja viestintä) työllisyys näyttäisi sen sijaan jo lähteneen kohentumaan. Odotamme, että ensi vuonna työllisyystilanne paranee myös jalostuksessa.

title: Reported Death of Uyghur Woman Detained Since Age 14
content:
The girl in the picture looking straight into the camera with probing eyes is 15-year-old Rahile Omer. She was photographed in March 2018 among hundreds of other detainees at a political re-education camp in Konasheher county, Kashgar, Xinjiang. A 2022 BBC investigation identified her as the youngest among the hundreds whose headshots were leaked in the Xinjiang Police Files. Previous records show authorities detained her at age 14 shortly after her parents’ detention in mid-2017.

On November 6, Radio Free Asia (RFA) reported that Rahile, at 23, had died in prison while serving an unjust 12-year sentence.

Human Rights Watch has not been able to independently verify this information, but the report should raise alarm about what is happening to the countless Uyghurs who remain behind bars as part of the Chinese government’s crimes against humanity since 2016.

title: Åbo Akademis och Kulturfondens storsatsning ska höja kompetensen i finska
content:
Allt färre elever har fungerande färdigheter i finska. Nu ska ett nytt projekt vid Åbo Akademi stödja lärare att utveckla undervisningen och stärka elevernas förmåga att använda finska. Svenska kulturfonden riktar sammanlagt 2,6 miljoner euro till satsningar på undervisningen i finska. 

Då elever får fler möjligheter att använda finska ökar självförtroendet och motivationen att lära sig. Det här är utgångspunkten för Åbo Akademis (ÅA) nya projekt Finska i lag.  

– Vi vill att unga ska våga tro på sina språkkunskaper och sin förmåga att lära sig mer, säger Michaela Pörn som är professor i finska språkets didaktik och prefekt för pedagogiska institutionen vid Åbo Akademi.   

Enligt Michaela Pörn finns det idag stora variationer mellan elevers kunskapsnivåer, förutsättningar för lärande och takt för språkutveckling

Här tar projektet Finska i lag, som Svenska kulturfonden finansierar med 1,2 miljoner euro, avstamp. Målet är att höja inlärningsresultaten i den grundläggande utbildningen och på andra stadiet i svenskspråkiga skolor i Finland.

title: Työelämän muuttuvat osaamistarpeet edellyttävät yrittäjyys- ja teknologiaosaamisen vahvistamista maatalousalan koulutuksessa
content:
Karvin arvioinnin mukaan maatalousalan tutkinnot tuottavat vahvaa käytännön ammattiosaamista ja hyviä työelämävalmiuksia. Kehittämistarpeita on erityisesti työelämässä oppimisen ohjauksessa, näyttöjen työelämälähtöisyydessä sekä yrittäjyys- ja teknologiaosaamisessa.

Kansallinen koulutuksen arviointikeskus (Karvi) toteutti vuonna 2026 maatalousalan perustutkinnon, ammattitutkinnon ja erikoisammattitutkinnon arvioinnin. Arvioinnissa tarkasteltiin pedagogista toimintaa, opiskelijoiden osaamista sekä koulutuksen tuottamia valmiuksia työelämään ja jatko-opintoihin. Arvioinnissa olivat mukana kaikki maatalousalan tutkintoja tarjoavat koulutuksen järjestäjät.

Arvioinnin mukaan opiskelijat pitävät työelämässä oppimista merkityksellisenä ammatillisen osaamisen kehittämisessä, mutta toteutuksessa on myös kehittämistarpeita. Erityisesti perustutkinto-opiskelijoiden työelämässä oppimisen aikaisessa ohjauksessa, tuessa ja osaamisen kehittymisen seurannassa on parannettavaa. Osa työpaikkaohjaajista kaipaa oppilaitoksilta nykyistä enemmän tukea opiskelijoiden ohjaamiseen ja osaamisen seurannan toteuttamiseen.

title: Digi- ja liikuntapedagogiikka lasten oppimisen ja osallisuuden tukena
content:
Mitä opiskelet ja kuinka kauan opinnot kestävät?

Opiskelen kasvatustieteiden maisteriksi varhaiskasvatuksen opintosuunnassa Helsingin yliopistossa. Aloitin opinnot elokuussa 2024 ja saan ne valmiiksi joulukuussa 2026, eli opintojen kokonaiskestoksi tulee vähän yli kaksi vuotta.

Kasvatustieteiden kandidaatiksi eli silloiseksi lastentarhanopettajaksi, nykyiseltä nimikkeeltäni varhaiskasvatuksen opettajaksi, valmistuin vuonna 2010. Valmistumisen jälkeen olen työskennellyt eri työnantajien, kuten kuntien, kaupunkien ja yksityisen palveluntuottajan, palveluksessa.

Minua ovat viime vuosina alkaneet kiinnostaa alan asiantuntijatyö ja hallinnollinen puoli, esimerkiksi johtaminen. Maisterin tutkinto avaa mahdollisuuksia työskennellä tällaisissa tehtävissä, ja siksi päätin lähteä jatkamaan opintojani.

Kuinka pitkä harjoittelujakso oli?

Opintoihini kuuluu pakollinen hallinnon ja kehittämistyön harjoittelu, jota pääsin suorittamaan tänne Heinolaan. Harjoittelu on pituudeltaan kolme kuukautta.

Mitä harjoittelujakso piti sisällään ja mikä oli sen lopputulos?

title: Demos-ohjelmassa entistä laajempi edustus
content:
Ryhmän puheenjohtaja Ella Turta pitää myönteisenä sitä, että yhä useammissa hankkeissa käsitellään yhteiskunnallisia kysymyksiä.

”Hakemuksista näkyy myös kasvava tarve yhteiskehittämiselle ja kansalaisyhteiskunnan kriisinkestävyyden vahvistamiselle, jolla voidaan lujittaa järjestöjen tärkeää roolia yhteiskunnallisessa vaikuttamisessa”, Turta sanoo. Hän toivoo, että ensi vuoden hakukierroksille osallistuisi vieläkin laajempi kirjo eri alojen järjestöjä.

Asiantuntijaryhmä on tietoinen Pohjolan maantieteellisen laajuuden aiheuttamista haasteista. Käytännön vaikeuksia aiheuttaa varsinkin pitkien etäisyyksien päässä olevien ihmisten saaminen yhteen. Samalla ryhmä korostaa, että Demos tukee myös Pohjolan arktisilla alueilla tehtävää yhteistyötä ja alkuperäiskansoihin liittyviä hankkeita.

Isompi ei myöskään aina ole parempi. Asiantuntijoiden mukaan ohjelmassa on tilaa myös kapea-alaisille, epätavallisille tai yllättäville hankkeille. Ryhmä arvostaa hakemuksia, joilla on selkeä tavoite ja joissa kuvataan selkeästi yhteistyökumppanit ja odotetut tulokset. Toteutustavan tulisi lisäksi olla innovatiivinen.

title: Kyrgyz Government Sold Mountain Resort to NGO Tied to Sanctioned Russian Influence Effort
content:
For years, the Bars resort, perched in the foothills above Kyrgyzstan’s iconic Issyk-Kul lake, attracted local and foreign visitors with its picturesque views and athletic facilities.

Few of them would have known that the resort, named after the mountainous Central Asian nation’s famous snow leopards, belonged to the family of the country’s most notorious criminal boss. 

Kamchi Kolbayev, the alleged head of a network involved in drug, arms, and human trafficking, extortion, and other crimes, was killed in a special operation by the Kyrgyz state security service (GKNB) in 2023. The agency subsequently released a video listing his seized assets, including the Bars complex.

In public remarks last month, Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov said his government had sold off the resort for $12 million, or double its value, to a local businessman. “That money went to the state budget,” Japarov said.

But an investigation by OCCRP has found that the government received no such windfall — the GKNB had originally valued the resort at $20 million — and that its actual buyer in 2025 was an obscure NGO with no website or public activity called Edinstvo Naroda (“Unity of the People”).

title: Inspiration from Charles Bukowski: You Might Be Old, Your Life May Be “Crappy,” But You Can Still Make Good Art
content:
Now more than ever, there’s tremendous pressure to make it big while you’re young.

Pity the 31-year-old who fails to make it onto a 30-under-30 list…

The soon-to-graduate high schooler passed over for YouTube stardom…

The great hordes who creep into middle age without so much as a TED Talk to their names…

Social media definitely magnifies the sensation that an unacceptable number of our peers have been granted first-class cabins aboard a ship that’s sailed without us. If we weren’t so demoralized, we’d sue Instagram for creating the impression that everyone else’s perfectly filtered life is leading to book deals and profiles in The New Yorker.

Don’t despair, dear reader. Charles Bukowski is about to make your day from beyond the grave.

In 1993, at the age of 73, the late writer and self-described “spoiled old toad,” took a break from recording the audiobook of Run With the Hunted to reflect upon his “crappy” life.

Some of these thoughts made it into Drew Christie’s animation, above, a reminder that the smoothest road isn’t always necessarily the richest one.

title: EU needs a system to respond to AI incidents, Finland and Estonia say
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Union should have a plan to respond to serious artificial intelligence incidents, two EU countries said ahead of a key Friday meeting of national leaders focused on AI.

In a letter seen by POLITICO, Finland and Estonia say the bloc “can still compete at the frontier” of AI by mobilizing capital and building up compute power, but this should go hand in hand with “governing it responsibly.”

The two countries, considered among Europe’s digital leaders, call for “EU-level arrangements for responding to serious AI incidents.”

AI safety and security are on Friday’s agenda of the first-ever European Council meeting devoted to the revolutionary new technology.

Concerns about whether Europe is prepared to respond to AI-powered threats have been picking up steam since a series of incidents this summer in which AI agents went rogue and hacked into other companies. Recent cyberattacks and revelations of coding vulnerabilities have also raised concerns that security systems must be better equipped for the arrival of artificial intelligence.

title: A Newborn Died in a Faith-Healing Sect. The State — and One Ex-Believer — Stepped in to Save Her Twin.
content:
The deputy medical examiner thought the family was being evasive. Eric Tonsfeldt had been dispatched to the pistachio-green house in Oregon City on the night of March 5, 2017. Inside he found Sarah Mitchell in bed, her dead newborn in her arms.

Mitchell is a member of the Followers of Christ, a sect known for refusing medical treatment. She had received no prenatal care. Three women without medical training guided her delivery that afternoon.

Tonsfeldt listened as the family insisted that the baby, whom they had named Ginnifer, had seemed healthy for most of the afternoon, then suddenly stopped breathing. They couldn’t explain why the baby appeared so underweight. Their answers to many of Tonsfeldt’s questions were vague. Nobody would make eye contact with him.

Later, investigators would discover that 13 minutes after Ginnifer’s birth, Followers began exchanging a series of worried texts. “Not good breathing,” one wrote in a group chat. Another requested prayers: “She’s really bad.” (One person in the chat would later advise deleting the messages.)

title: How years of research built Grand Theft Auto VI’s obsessively detailed world
content:
The developers behind its virtual Florida share how they built their most ambitious world so far

• Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

In 2015, a group of Grand Theft Auto developers from Rockstar North took their first trips to Miami to do field research for the next game in the phenomenally popular crime series. “Before you’re doing hyper-organised research trips, you’re immersing yourself in the place and its history, the vibe of it,” Rob Nelson, one of the lead developers on GTA VI, tells me. “[You see] the physical places you want to move characters through, the experiences you want them to have, and the juxtaposition between the extremes of society that are in Miami.”

I wondered: did people ever recognise them on any of their research trips? Did locals know what they were doing? This is the biggest game in the world, after all; I imagine it would be difficult to go entirely undercover. “We’re always semi-undercover,” he says. “But if you have a bunch of dorks going through a terrifying neighbourhood, you do stick out a bit.”

title: Stubb: 1,5 asteen rajan ylittyminen on hiuskarvan varassa
content:
Pariisin ilmastosopimuksen 1,5 asteen rajan ylittyminen on hiuskarvan varassa, sanoi presidentti Alexander Stubb keskiviikkona YK:n COP31-ilmastokokouksessa Turkissa Suomen kansallisessa puheenvuorossa.

- Tiede ei jätä liikkumavaraa passiivisuudelle. Vähintään tilapäinen 1,5 asteen rajan rikkoutuminen on todennäköistä, mutta tämän ylityksen kesto ja mittakaava riippuu päätöksistämme, Stubb sanoi puhujanlavalla Turkin Antalyassa.

Pariisin ilmastosopimuksessa vuonna 2015 sovittiin, että maat pyrkivät rajoittamaan ilmaston lämpenemisen 1,5 asteeseen esiteollisen ajan keskiarvoon verrattuna.

Puheessaan Stubb valitteli sitä, että Ukrainan sota ja muut konfliktit ovat vieneet huomiota ilmastonmuutokselta.

Euroopan komission puheenjohtaja Ursula von der Leyen varoitti puheessaan, että maailma maksaa kovaa hintaa siitä, että status quo -tilanteesta pidetään kiinni.

- Olemme menossa yli 1,5 asteen rajan, ja jokaisella asteen murto-osalla on väliä, von der Leyen sanoi.

PRESIDENTTI Stubbin mukaan ilmastonmuutoksen ratkaisuun tarvitaan multilateralismia eli monenkeskistä kansainvälistä yhteistyötä.

title: I Came for the Learning, Left with a Renewed Purpose: My Transformative Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0 Experience
content:
Some experiences stay with you long after the event has ended. They are not just about the knowledge acquired or the activities undertaken; they are about the people you meet, the connections you build, the ideas you exchange, and the renewed sense of purpose you take home. For me, Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0 was one of such experiences.

Organised by African & Proud, under the leadership of its co-founders, Richard Edozie and Kolawole Oyewole, Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0 brought together young people, passionate Wikimedians, knowledge enthusiasts, and emerging changemakers in Lagos, Nigeria, for an enriching experience centred on open knowledge, leadership, collaboration, and capacity development.

Having participated in Afroyanga Bootcamp 2.0, returning for the third edition was particularly exciting. It was another opportunity to reconnect with the Afroyanga experience, meet new people, share experiences, and continue growing within a community that inspires young Africans to contribute meaningfully to the knowledge ecosystem.

title: Belgium's own ICE could be the first of many in Europe
content: Only 16% of third-country nationals (people not from the EU or EEA) who were ordered to leave Belgium in 2025 actually did so. To raise that number, the Belgian parliament passed the “home raids law” last week. It allows police officers, with authorisation from a judge, to enter private homes and arrest foreign nationals who have refused an order to leave the country and are considered a risk to “public order” or “national security”. In protest against the new measure, 3,000 people formed a human chain around the Palace of Justice in Brussels and demonstrations took place in some 60 municipalities. Activists compare the law to the practices of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). In fact, all of the EU is moving the same way. In force since October, the EU Return Regulation allows for home searches of people without their consent. title: What lurks ‘Below’ Newfoundland waters? A marine biologist explains the science behind the show
content:
When I learned that Netflix planned to film the miniseries Below, about a sea monster terrorizing a Newfoundland outport, I thought to myself: “THIS I’ve gotta see!”

First, the series showcases coastal Newfoundland, where I was raised and live. Second, I have studied ocean life in the island’s waters for most of my career. Third, it features the marine lab where I work, the Oceans Sciences Centre. And fourth, it stars a giant squid(-ish) animal (sorry Josh Hartnett).

Giant squid have a special place in Newfoundland folklore and science, from early encounters with fishermen to some of the first scientific evidence of their existence.

One key player in this history was the Irish clergyman Moses Harvey, who moved to Newfoundland in 1852 and undertook natural history research in what was then a British colony.

Harvey’s research included revealing the existence of giant squid to the world based on a specimen that washed ashore. Fishermen had brought it to him to photograph and communicate to the science community in London.

title: Silicon Valley Podcast Hosts Try to Understand Why Regular People Are Mad
content:
If you want to watch four billionaire/billionaire wannabes cope with the election results, you could watch the absolutely dreadful hosts of All-In talk across a livestream and a follow-up podcast for four hours, or you could just watch the Lucille Bluth “What could a banana cost, Michael,” clip on repeat until your eyes and ears bleed.

Throughout their post-election breakdown podcast episode released over the weekend, the All-In bros seem to be on the verge of grasping why Americans are so mad and who they’re mad at, but are still trying to find the guy who did this. They appear to finally grasp that Americans are mad at something called “oligarchs” but largely do not seem to know who they are (it’s them). Populist anger at the oligarchs is a “perception” or “narrative” problem. The four hosts — David Sacks, Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, and David Friedberg— spend much of the episode considering whether they are out of touch, or whether the children are wrong. Let’s see how they did.
