title: "American Scoundrel": From Roy Cohn to Stephen Miller, "McCarthyism Lives On," Says Author Kai Bird
content:
We speak with historian Kai Bird about American Scoundrel, a new biography of the notorious political fixer Roy Cohn, who rose to fame as chief counsel to Joe McCarthy during the senator’s anti-communist campaign, served as a lawyer for the New York mob, and was an influential voice in Republican circles until his death from AIDS-related complications in 1986. His most impactful relationship, however, would prove to be with a young Donald Trump, whom he mentored in business and politics during the 1970s and ’80s.

Facing political setbacks during his first term as president, Trump reportedly asked, “Where’s my Roy Cohn?” Bird, who co-authored American Scoundrel with his wife Susan Goldmark, says Trump may have found his Cohn in Stephen Miller, the architect of the administration’s mass deportation policies whom Trump just elevated to chief of staff.

“It’s not really a surprise that, cornered and wounded by the recent election results, he reaches out and pulls up Stephen Miller, who’s very similar in his willingness to go on the offensive and never back down, and to say outrageous things to try to change the narrative,” says Bird.

title: Zahedan: Three Citizens Killed in Indiscriminate Shooting by Military Forces
content:
According to HRANA, citing the Balochistan Human Rights Documentation Network, three citizens were killed as a result of gunfire by military forces in Zahedan.

Two of the victims have been identified as Omid Jamalzehi, 30, married and a resident of Harmak in Zahedan, and Hanzaleh Jamalzehi, 32,  father of four children, and a resident of Zahedan.

According to the report, the three citizens were traveling from Tehran to Zahedan when, at approximately 3:00 a.m. on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, military forces opened fire on their vehicle in the Lakhshak area, part of Harmak Rural District in Zahedan, without ordering the vehicle to stop or issuing any warning. The occupants of the Peugeot vehicle were struck by gunfire, bringing the vehicle to a halt.

The report further states that, according to eyewitnesses, after the vehicle stopped, military forces fired at Hanzaleh Jamalzehi and another occupant before leaving the scene.

Following calls from local residents to emergency services, the bodies of the three victims were transported by ambulance to the forensic medical facility. Family members and relatives of the victims gathered outside the forensic medical facility in Zahedan.

title: Kysynnän välittyminen työllisyydeksi eri toimialoilla
content: Tässä tutkimuksessa tehdään staattisella panos-tuotosmallilla laskelmat siitä, kuinka suuri jalanjälki työllisyyteen Suomen kansantalouden eri loppukysyntäerillä oli vuosina 2008, 2014, 2019 ja 2023. Laskelmassa huomioidaan myös toimialojen väliset välituotevirrat. Neljän eri lopputuotekysyntäerän työllisyysvaikutukset suuntautuvat eri toimialoille. Yksityisessä kulutuksessa valtaosa kysynnästä suuntautuu yksityisiin palveluihin, julkisessa kulutuksessa julkiseen palvelutuotantoon, pääoman bruttomuodostuksessa rakentamiseen ja yksityisiin tukipalveluihin sekä kokonaisviennissä teollisuuteen, informaatio- ja viestintäalaan sekä yksityisiin tukipalveluihin. Yhteiskunta on palveluvaltaistunut, ja työllisyysjalanjälki onkin kasvanut julkisissa palveluissa, ammatillisessa, tieteellisessä ja teknisessä toiminnassa, hallinto- ja tukipalvelutoiminnassa sekä informaatio- ja viestintäalalla. Teollisuudessa jalanjälki väheni ensin, mutta on ollut vakaa vuoden 2014 jälkeen. Julkisen kulutuksen merkitys kokonaistyöllisyydessä on noussut yksityisen kulutuksen ohitse. Muutokset heijastavat talouden kysyntä- ja tuotantorakenteiden sekä tuontialttiuden muutoksia mutta myös tuottavuuskehitystä eri aloilla.

title: New Master’s Programme in One Health to train experts for health threats that cross disciplines and borders
content:
“Covid made me realise how little I actually knew about other fields,” says Tarja Sironen, Professor of Emerging Infectious Diseases at the University of Helsinki.

During the pandemic, virologists like Sironen suddenly had to work with social scientists, lawyers and physicists. Even explaining how the virus spread through the air required expertise from several disciplines at once.

The pandemic also showed how quickly a health threat can grow into an economic and societal crisis, and how much trust can be lost along the way. Ministries have since said openly that they wish experts capable of working across disciplines already existed. Few graduates today are trained for such work. The new Master’s Programme in One Health, launching at the University of Helsinki in autumn 2027, aims to close this gap.

Unlike most health-related master’s programmes, the new programme will bring together students and researchers from six faculties. After learning the foundations in One Health, students will choose their focus from eight thematic areas, such as infectious disease dynamics, food and water safety, environmental health, or governance and policy.

title: Hope for World’s Forests and Their Defenders at COP31
content:
The Netherlands’ commitment at the United Nations climate change conference (COP31) today that it will invest up to half a billion dollars in the Tropical Forest Forever Facility (TFFF) is a major step towards protecting the world’s most biodiverse ecosystems and the rights and livelihoods of millions of people who depend on them. 

When I attended COP26 in Glasgow in 2021, 137 countries committed to halt and reverse forest loss and land degradation by 2030. While that list of signatories has grown, the funding needed to meet these goals has remained inadequate. This endangers our collective ability to ensure forests, which absorb and store planet warming emissions, can act as an emergency brake to the climate crisis.

The TFFF seeks to tackle that problem by pooling money from governments and private actors to invest in a profit-yielding fund; the profit then supports payments for eligible tropical countries that demonstrably protect their forests. The goal is to have a self-sustaining fund that sidesteps the capricious ebbs and flows of aid. Initially championed by Brazil, it is now financially backed by multiple governments and private actors.

content:
Suomen venäjänkieliset 2026 –selvityksestä käy ilmi, että Suomessa asuvien venäjänkielisten luottamuksen heikkeneminen yhteiskunnan instituutioihin on pääosin pysähtynyt vuoden 2024 selvityksen tasolle. Luottamus on kuitenkin edelleen monilta osin vuoden 2022 Suomen venäjänkieliset -selvityksen tasoa matalampaa.

Kyselyyn vastanneista 82 prosenttia kokee olonsa kotoisaksi omalla asuinalueellaan. Suomalaisen yhteiskunnan osaksi itsensä kokee 59 prosenttia. Sen sijaan 36 prosenttia kokee kuuluvansa Suomessa asuvaan venäjänkieliseen yhteisöön.

Yhteiskunnallisten asioiden aktiivinen seuraaminen on pysynyt lähes ennallaan vuodesta 2024: vuonna 2026 niitä seurasi aktiivisesti 46 prosenttia vastaajista, kun vuonna 2024 osuus oli 47 prosenttia.

Sen sijaan yhteiskunnallisia asioita passiivisesti seuraavien osuus on kasvanut tasaisesti: vuonna 2022 heitä oli 19 prosenttia, vuonna 2024 jo 26 prosenttia ja vuonna 2026 yhteensä 30 prosenttia. Aktiivisen seuraamisen suhteellisen matala taso on huomionarvoinen yhteiskunnallisen osallisuuden näkökulmasta.

title: Tutkimus: Esihenkilön tekoälyosaamisella vahva yhteys työntekijöiden tekoälyn käytön aktiivisuuteen
content:
Tekoäly muuttaa työelämää nopeasti, mutta muutos ei näytä etenevän samalla vauhdilla organisaation kaikilla tasoilla. Jabran maailmanlaajuisessa tutkimuksessa ylimmän johdon edustajista 30 prosenttia käyttää tekoälyä useita kertoja päivässä. Työntekijöistä, joilla ei ole esihenkilövastuuta, näin tekee vain kahdeksan prosenttia.

Jabra Research Instituten WorkLife 2026: The New Shape of Work -raporttia varten haastateltiin yli 6 000 tietotyöläistä Saksassa, Yhdysvalloissa, Isossa-Britanniassa, Ranskassa, Puolassa ja Intiassa.

Tutkimuksessa tekoälyn aktiivikäyttäjiksi määritellään työntekijät, jotka käyttävät tekoälyä työssään useita kertoja päivässä. Tekoälyä vähän käyttävät puolestaan käyttävät sitä korkeintaan kerran kuukaudessa.

Ero johdon ja muiden työntekijöiden välillä näkyy myös vähän tekoälyä käyttävien määrässä. Työntekijöistä, joilla ei ole esihenkilövastuuta, 40 prosenttia käyttää tekoälyä korkeintaan kerran kuukaudessa. Ylimmän johdon edustajista näin harvoin tekoälyä käyttää vain 14 prosenttia.

title: European gaming firms say new EU consumer rules will ‘cripple’ the industry
content:
BRUSSELS — Top global gaming companies have blasted new EU consumer regulations they say would “cripple the competitiveness of Europe’s world-leading video games industry.”

The European Commission unveiled a new set of rules Wednesday on consumer protection, including the Digital Fairness Act, that is part of the first-ever sector-specific limits on the video-game industry, alongside the EU’s mid-September regulation to protect children online.

Under the proposed DFA, which still has to be negotiated with other EU institutions, video games would no longer be able to earn money by offering minors micro-transactions to advance in the game, known as pay-to-win or pay-to-progress. There are also restrictions on “loot boxes,” which contain surprise virtual items that players can buy with real money. The law also stipulates that in-app virtual currencies must be turned off by default for under-18s.

The Commission says these practices encourage overspending, which is especially dangerous for vulnerable consumers like kids. Violating the rules can lead to fines of up to 6% of global revenue in cases that affect more than two-thirds of the EU population.

title: Prophecy, Scorn and a Rejection of This World: The Forbidding Vision of a Faith-Healing Preacher
content:
It was a stark and forbidding vision for those who followed the righteous path. Scorn, the preacher told his congregation, was a person’s lot if they led an “honest, clean, pure, godly life.” The world hated “people that live like that,” he said.

“They want you to be just as ungodly and filthy as they are,” he said in a rare audio recording, obtained by The Oregonian/OregonLive, of a 1958 sermon.

The preacher was Walter White, who led an Oregon City offshoot of the Followers of Christ, an Idaho sect that spurns medical treatment as a show of faith. White was a grocer, originally from Picabo, Idaho, whose congregants came to view as a prophet. He rambled at times during his sermon but always returned to simple and severe messages about choosing righteousness rather than the ways of the world. A trim figure in wire-rim glasses and dark combed-back hair, he spoke in a voice that evoked the stentorian tones of an old newsreel announcer. In the scratchy recording, people cough and babies cry as he preaches.

title: AI datacentres plan on-site power stations on huge scale despite climate risks, research reveals
content:
181GW of gas-fired capacity proposed for sites in US and Europe because of delays in connecting to national grids, says report

Developers of AI datacentres plan to build on-site climate-destroying gas power stations on a huge scale to meet their energy demands, research reveals.

Datacentres planned across the US, the UK and mainland Europe have proposals to build fossil fuel plants on-site to create 181GW of gas-fired capacity because of delays to connect to national grids, according to the findings. This is almost four times the total peak electricity demand of Great Britain.

title: Germany’s Freedom of Information Under Renewed Attack
content:
A leaked draft of the Interior Ministry’s proposed Law on the Adjustment of Transparency, Disclosure, and Information Duties to Ensure Adequate Protection of Critical Infrastructure was made public on November 5, reigniting concerns about a renewed attack on freedom of information in Germany.  

The government’s previous attempt in June to introduce a law that would essentially gut the Freedom of Information Act stalled, after wide pushback from civil society and even from within the Social Democrats—a partner in the coalition government.  

A new government draft law dated September 30 now proposes to amend the Freedom of Information Act by excluding its application to any information requests about state actions relating to “critical infrastructure” or infrastructure deemed “in particular need of protection to maintain public security.” These vague provisions would give authorities that receive freedom of information requests broad discretionary powers to reject requests.

title: “We Have No One”: How Trump’s Dismantling of the VA Left a Veterans Hospital in Crisis
content:
John Falchetto was a survivor. In Vietnam, his river gunboat came under devastating rocket fire. He was the only one to make it out alive. But this February, Falchetto, who had just turned 80, began to have piercing stomach pains. He was in distress for days. Finally, Falchetto went to the VA hospital in East Orange, New Jersey.

A CT scan of Falchetto’s abdomen suggested his appendix had not only burst, but that it was gangrenous. His gut was so filled with bacteria and pus that tissue was dying. Doctors wrote that he needed surgery immediately.

But that night, the hospital’s operating room was closed. Months earlier, the ventilation system had malfunctioned, and the repair team was short-staffed. So Falchetto lay there, his life in the balance, for seven hours.

This was not normal. But nothing had been normal at East Orange since President Donald Trump returned to office last year and set his sights on the VA.

title: When does difficult behaviour become a UCoC concern?
content:
During a Wikimedia workshop, an experienced contributor repeatedly interrupts a newbie and dismisses their questions. Later, the newbie privately tells the facilitator that they no longer feel comfortable participating. What should the organiser do?

This was one of the situations explored during the EduWiki x VSN Workshop, Creating Safer and More Inclusive Wikimedia Spaces: Understanding and Applying the Universal Code of Conduct. Held on 15 October 2026, the online session brought together 56 participants from Central & Eastern Europe & Central Asia (CEECA), East, Southeast Asia and the Pacific (ESEAP), Middle East and North Africa (MENA), North America (NA), Northern and Western Europe (NWE), South Asia (SA) and the Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) regions, and was organised by the EduWiki Hub in collaboration with the Volunteer Supporters Network (VSN) and the Wikimedia Foundation’s Universal Code of Conduct Coordinating Committee (U4C).

The workshop looked at how the Universal Code of Conduct (UCoC) applies to Wikimedia projects, events, education programmes and community spaces, with practical discussions about recognising concerning behaviour and deciding how to respond.

Karvin arvioinnin mukaan maatalousalan tutkinnot tuottavat vahvaa käytännön ammattiosaamista ja hyviä työelämävalmiuksia. Kehittämistarpeita on erityisesti työelämässä oppimisen ohjauksessa, näyttöjen työelämälähtöisyydessä sekä yrittäjyys- ja teknologiaosaamisessa.

Kansallinen koulutuksen arviointikeskus (Karvi) toteutti vuonna 2026 maatalousalan perustutkinnon, ammattitutkinnon ja erikoisammattitutkinnon arvioinnin. Arvioinnissa tarkasteltiin pedagogista toimintaa, opiskelijoiden osaamista sekä koulutuksen tuottamia valmiuksia työelämään ja jatko-opintoihin. Arvioinnissa olivat mukana kaikki maatalousalan tutkintoja tarjoavat koulutuksen järjestäjät.

Arvioinnin mukaan opiskelijat pitävät työelämässä oppimista merkityksellisenä ammatillisen osaamisen kehittämisessä, mutta toteutuksessa on myös kehittämistarpeita. Erityisesti perustutkinto-opiskelijoiden työelämässä oppimisen aikaisessa ohjauksessa, tuessa ja osaamisen kehittymisen seurannassa on parannettavaa. Osa työpaikkaohjaajista kaipaa oppilaitoksilta nykyistä enemmän tukea opiskelijoiden ohjaamiseen ja osaamisen seurannan toteuttamiseen.

title: AI has made it ‘close to impossible’ to assess university coursework, regulator says
content:
Office for Students says institutions in England should return to traditional exams and in-person presentations

Universities should go back to traditional exams and in-person presentations to grade students after lecturers complained that AI has made it “close to impossible” to assess coursework, according to an investigation by England’s higher education regulator.

The Office for Students (OfS) said the credibility of degrees from England’s universities was under threat from the prolific use of AI in essays, dissertations and “open book” exams, with students reporting that their peers boasted of using AI undetected by staff.

title: The AI Safety Debate Has Lost the Plot. We Asked 10 Experts What the Real Nightmares Are
content:
How should people think about AI safety?
Some of the comparisons that people draw between AI and nuclear are quite frustrating. Despite constantly comparing AI to nuclear, they’re denying standard risk assessment techniques as being sufficient to control AI. I wrote an entire paper on this.

Part of this field of risk assessment was born out of the Manhattan Project. Scientists were very concerned, and they developed rigorous standards around systems to limit harm to human life, the environment, and even financial and national security assets. They came up with methods for assessing safety that were ultimately based on answering a democratic question: How safe is safe enough? That is the question that any safety engineer has to ask, and is core to everything that follows.

title: 2027 Public Domain Film Contest: The Internet Archive is Looking For Creative Short Films Made By You!
content:
We invite filmmakers, artists, and creatives of all skill levels and backgrounds to celebrate Public Domain Day, by creating and uploading a short film not exceeding 4 minutes to the Internet Archive.

This contest offers a chance to explore and reimagine the creative treasures entering the public domain, especially works from 1931 that enter the public domain on January 1—classic literature, early sound films, cartoons, music, and art. Participants are encouraged to use materials from the Internet Archive’s collections to craft unique films that breathe new life into these cultural gems.

Top entries will be awarded prizes up to $2,000, with winners announced during our in-person Public Domain Day Celebration on January 27, 2027. All submissions will be featured in a special Public Domain Day Collection on archive.org and highlighted in a January 2027 blog post.

Join us in this creative celebration of cultural heritage and timeless art!

title: Managing Russia’s Military-Industrial Degradation: Navigating Wartime Industrial Constraints, Stockpile Exhaustion, and Hardware Attrition
content:
• This paper assesses Russia’s near-term domestic defense-industrial capacity and the ability of the military-industrial complex (OPK) to meet the increasing demands of the war against Ukraine.
  • Four years into the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Russia has not solved the problem of sustaining wartime production. Instead, the Kremlin has only postponed addressing the OPK’s many problems.
  • Output constraints are increasingly defining the OPK’s future: exhaustion (specifically, the depletion of existing stockpiles and the constant need to repair damaged equipment and refurbish Soviet-legacy hardware taken out of storage) and attrition (the limited ability to produce new military hardware domestically faster than it is consumed).
  • Finding a balance between the two constraints has allowed the armed forces to continue fielding equipment, but it has also accelerated the depletion of Soviet-era reserves. However, the constant trade-off has become a systemic condition that defines the current and future trajectory of the military industry. The OPK cannot indefinitely compensate for battlefield losses through repair and refurbishment alone.
snippet: This paper assesses Russia’s near-term domestic defense-industrial capacity and the ability of the military-industrial complex (OPK) to meet the increasing demands of the war against Ukraine.

title: Commissioner Micallef announces EU Culture Dialogue Community
content:
On 12 November 2026, Glenn Micallef European Commissioner for Intergenerational Fairness, Youth, Culture and Sport, held the first EU Culture Dialogue Annual Meeting. The event marks the first anniversary of the adoption of the Culture Compass for Europe.

At the meeting, Commissioner Micallef introduced the EU Culture Dialogue Community. The Commissioner is inviting organisations in the cultural and creative sectors to become part of a community of stakeholders that will be informed and consulted on developments in EU cultural policy and forthcoming relevant initiatives.

The EU Culture Dialogue Community is a new way for the cultural and creative sectors to help shape European cultural policy.

  • Register to become part of the EU Culture Dialogue Community (external link)

    • Representatives of Europe’s cultural and creative sectors spent the day discussing with Commissioner Micallef key actions of the Culture Compass for Europe for 2027, including an EU Artists’ Charter, an AI strategy for the cultural and creative sectors, and a new report on the state of culture in the EU, with a specific emphasis on artistic freedom.

title: Türkiye is leading climate talks while burning coal
content: COP31 host, Türkiye, is one of the world's 10 largest coal consumers. One of the main themes of the COP31 action agenda is electrification: replacing fossil fuels with electricity in sectors such as transport and industry. But electrification only cuts emissions if the electricity itself is clean, and in Türkiye coal is still the main source of electricity. Türkiye has pledged to speed up electrification, with a proposed national target of raising electricity's share of final energy consumption to 35% by 2035. Climate and energy campaigner at Greenpeace Türkiye, Emel Türker Alpay, told TEC the country's coal strategy is a short-sighted way of pursuing energy independence. It's also costly: the government provides around €2.4 billion a year in subsidies and incentives to support coal, aiming to boost domestic output, reduce dependence on energy imports, and protect jobs in coal-producing regions. And because some of that coal is imported, she argued, it does little to make Türkiye energy-independent. And the cost of dependence is rising. title: Join the Webinar “Climate Change and Spatial Planning on the Baltic Sea Coast: Where Are We Now?”
content:

Organised within the Baltic PlaNet project platform, this event launches an online webinar series designed to support spatial planners in addressing climate change risks in their work, foster exchange of experience and strengthen cooperation among planners across the Baltic Sea Region, contributing to more climate-resilient Baltic Sea coasts.

As the first in a series of Baltic PlaNet webinars, this webinar will focus on basics of climate science, introducing with observed climate trends and the impacts of climate change in the Baltic Sea Region. This will be followed by short presentations from spatial planners working in coastal areas across the Baltic Sea Region, sharing their observations and experiences of how climate change is affecting coastal areas, what challenges it creates, and how these are (or should be) addressed through spatial planning and coastal management.

title: In Conversation with Sandra Benčić, Croatia
content:
Sandra Bencic ©️ European Greens / Margot L’Hermite

Sandra Benčić is a Croatian politician and legal expert who graduated from the Faculty of Law at the University of Zagreb. She demonstrated an early interest in human rights during her university education and subsequently pursued a career in civil society organisations. Benčić is one of the founders and coordinators of the Green-Left political party Možemo!. Since the 2020 national parliamentary elections, she has been serving as the president of the Možemo! parliamentary group and has acted as the Chair of the Environment and Nature Conservation Committee in the Croatian Parliament. Her main areas of work concern environmental protection, transparency, and fair economic policies.

In this interview by Jamie Kendrick, Sandra Benčić reflects on Možemo!’s rise from a grassroots Zagreb initiative to one of Croatia’s leading political forces. She discusses the movement’s key electoral breakthroughs, strategy for broadening support, vision for a fair green economy, and ambitions to build a progressive majority in Croatia and Europe.

Why did you choose the name Možemo!, and what does it tell us about the movement?

title: OPINION: Ukraine’s Black Soil and the Hidden Reality of a Ruined Country
content:
By Wolfgang Bittner*

GÖTTINGEN, Germany | 10 November 2026 (IDN) — Ukraine, which has been at war with Russia since Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, is known for its fertile black soil—chernozem—a nutrient-rich humus soil that in some areas reaches considerable depth and produces high agricultural yields.

Chernozem covers a substantial part of Ukraine, particularly in the east and south. Ukraine possesses tens of millions of hectares of agricultural land and one of the world’s largest concentrations of black soil.

Ukraine is also the second-largest country in Europe after Russia. In recent years, its extensive mineral resources—including coal, iron ore, lithium, graphite, manganese, oil and natural gas—have increasingly become a subject of international interest.

Less attention is paid to the strategic importance of its agricultural land. Before the war, Ukraine was among the world’s leading exporters of corn and wheat and held important shares of global markets for barley, sunflower oil and rapeseed.

Before the full-scale war, Ukraine routinely produced around 60 million tonnes or more of grain annually, mainly corn, wheat and barley, with a large proportion exported.

title: Better Late than Never: Ten Years On, Time to Put the e-Lending Ruling into Law
content:
Ten years ago today, the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) determined that a library lending an e-Book is, in law, a library lending a physical book. A decade later, libraries are still waiting for the law to say so. Legislators at EU and national levels have proven stubbornly resistant to efforts to get them to fulfil their obligations to uphold and abide by EU law, encouraged by those who gain from the status quo.

This is not for want of a need for change. Since 2016, the arguments and evidence for a sound and simple legal basis for e-Lending in Europe have kept piling up.

On the 10th anniversary of the Vereniging Openbare Bibliotheken (VOB) vs Stichting Leenrecht judgement, we look back at what the Court said, why it matters, and how the upcoming copyright reform in the EU offers a way to do better for Europe’s researchers, learners, teachers and readers.

The VOB case stemmed from uncertainty in the Netherlands about whether the lending of e-Books could take place under the EU’s existing Rental and Lending Directive.

title: Taideteoskuvat taidemuseon näyttelyjulkaisussa edellyttivät luvan ja korvauksen
content:
Tekijänoikeusneuvosto on antanut lausunnon Serlachius-museon Catch-julkaisusta Kuvaston pyynnöstä. Lausunnon perusteella taideteoskuvien käyttö näyttelyjulkaisussa ei ollut vapaata tekijänoikeuslain rajoitussäännösten nojalla.

Kuvasto pyysi keväällä 2026 tekijänoikeusneuvostolta lausuntoa, onko Catch-julkaisu tekijänoikeuslain tarkoittama näyttelyluettelo. Gösta Serlachiuksen taidesäätiö julkaisi myyntiin tarkoitetun kirjan museonäyttelyn yhteydessä.

Tekijänoikeuslaki sallii näyttelyssä esillä olevan teoksen kuvaamisen näyttelyä koskevaan tiedotukseen tai näyttelyluetteloon. Näyttelyluettelolla tai -katalogilla tarkoitetaan teosluetteloa, joka palvelee teoksia katsomaan tulevan yleisön opastusta, ja se voidaan valmistaa ilman taiteilijan suostumusta ja korvausta.

Tekijänoikeusneuvoston 10.11.2026 julkaistun lausunnon mukaan taidemuseon julkaisua ei voida pitää näyttelyn tiedottamisena eikä luettelona. Neuvosto katsoo, että esseitä ja runomuotoisia tekstejä sisältävä näyttelyjulkaisu rinnastuu ennemmin tavanomaiseen taidekirjaan.

title: Keniassa onnistuttiin kuvaamaan korallien kutemista – Se voi auttaa riuttojen pelastamisessa
content:
Kymmenen yötä pilkkopimeässä vedessä tuotti vihdoin tulosta. Lokakuun alussa tutkijat onnistuivat videokuvaamaan korallien kutemista ensimmäistä kertaa pariinkymmeneen vuoteen.

Korallien kutuaikatauluja on kartoitettu aiemminkin ja ne tunnetaan suuressa osassa maailmaa, mutta Kenian rannikolla Intian valtameren korallien aiemmat tiedot olivat suunnilleen vuosituhannen alusta, eikä tarkkaa kutemisaikaa ole ollut tiedossa.

Iso osa koralleista kutee vain muutaman tunnin ajan auringon laskettua, usein muutama päivä täydenkuun jälkeen. Ilman aiempaa täsmällistä tietoa kutemista on äärimmäisen vaikea nähdä. Nyt kun tietoa on viimein saatu videokuvan ansiosta, tutkijat aikovat kartoittaa Kenian korallien kutemisaikataulua tarkemmin. Tutkimustyötä tehdään tulevina kuukausina.

”Madagaskarin korallit kutevat lokakuusta huhtikuuhun, mutta Kenian korallit eivät seuraa samaa kaavaa”, kertoo tutkijatohtori Juliet Karisa Kenian meri- ja kalatalouden tutkimuslaitokselta Mombasasta.

Katso alla olevalta videolta miten korallit kutevat!

title: Sharing the Value of AI training
content:
Today we publish Sharing the value of AI training: a collective remuneration mechanism, a discussion paper and our contribution to the European Commission’s targeted consultation on a better copyright environment for European creativity and innovation.

The paper builds on Beyond AI and Copyright, which we published in June 2025, and follows the call for a European content levy that Mistral made earlier this year. It sets out, as a basis for discussion, a more detailed mechanism tied to the training of AI models and built with the instruments of EU copyright and market-access law.

In its call for evidence, the Commission states that it wants to “improve the conditions for creators’ remuneration, while making it easier for providers of generative AI to access copyright-protected content”. These objectives pull in different directions. Measures aimed at one tend to come at the cost of the other: stricter reservation regimes make access to data for AI development harder, while broader exceptions leave rightholders without remuneration.

title: Open Source AI Salons: Shaping the OSAID, Together
content:
Two years after the release of the Open Source AI Definition (OSAID 1.0), the Open Source Initiative hosted the first in a series of Open Source AI Salons, gatherings to discuss the future of the OSAID. In collaboration with key partners in Raleigh and Barcelona, the events brought together civil society, government, industry, and academia to understand the practical application of the OSAID.

These interdisciplinary, community-driven events provide the ground to surface challenges, examine assumptions, and explore practical issues affecting the Open Source community when it comes to AI. As we head into 2027, we are developing opportunities to bring candid discussions about the OSAID to more people in more places. OSI is steadfast in its commitment to empowering the Open Source community and promoting a healthy Open Source AI ecosystem.

title: How decades of US ‘forever war’ led to the Republicans’ midterm losses
content:
After the 1991 Gulf War, Saddam Hussein, the former president of Iraq, declared “dignified victory” despite a military defeat. He had survived the invasion, while his adversary George HW Bush was facing a recession at home. Bush would go on to lose the 1992 elections to Bill Clinton, who swept to victory with the slogan: “It’s the economy, stupid”.

Even with Iraq’s armed forces devastated, Saddam was able to frame the military defeat as success: not even a coalition of 42 nations could unseat him. Following huge Republican losses in the 2026 US midterm elections, the Islamic Republic of Iran could claim a similar victory, even with the death of its Supreme Leader, Ali Khamenei.

In 2024, Donald Trump ran on an electoral promise of “no more wars”. Two years later, American voters dealt his party a resounding defeat. Not only did Trump begin a war with Iran, but that war is fast becoming another “forever war” with no clear end in sight.

title: Economic coercion once ousted Iran’s leader – but that was the 1950s; don’t expect a repeat today
content:
“Very little gets into, or out of, Iran!” President Donald Trump claimed on Nov. 8, 2026, in a social media post that also lauded “history’s greatest Naval Blockade.”

It followed the unveiling of Task Force Iron Gate – the Trump administration’s latest plan to isolate the Iranian economy in a bid to coerce the government in Tehran to bend to Washington’s will. At the same time, Trump has suggested that a return to open war with Iran is “highly unlikely.”

From my perspective as an expert on Iran’s relations with the wider world, I believe that the U.S. war in Iran – now into its ninth month – is increasingly resembling an earlier episode of Iranian-Western conflict. In the early 1950s, the British imposed a two-year blockade and embargo against Iran after Iran’s then-prime minister, Mohammad Mossadegh, nationalized the country’s U.K.-controlled oil industry.

These efforts culminated in a 1953 British- and American-backed plot to stir up protest in Iran and eventually overthrow Mossadegh.

title: A data management plan is a good idea. But which tool should you use?
content:
You have been told by the funder that your research project needs a Data Management Plan, or DMP.

Fair enough.

Then you start looking for a tool to create one.

Suddenly there is ARGOS. DMPonline. DMPTool. RDMO. Data Stewardship Wizard. easyDMP. GFBio DMP Tool. DataPLAN. ARIADNE. And several more.

They all seem to help with data management planning, but they are not all designed for the same researchers, disciplines, or workflows.

So where do you start?

A Data Management Plan helps you think through what will happen to your research data during and beyond a project.

  • How will the data be organised and documented?
  • Where will it be stored?
  • Who can access it?
  • Which standards should be used?
  • What happens when the project ends?

    • The questions may be similar across disciplines, but the answers often are not.

    A researcher working with natural science collections may need to think about specimen data, metadata standards, persistent identifiers, sensitive locality information, or data publication.

    An archaeologist may have different disciplinary requirements.

    Plant scientists may work with specialised templates and infrastructures.

title: Analysis: Which countries have sent the most delegates to COP31?
content:
More than 92,000 people have registered to attend the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, potentially making it the largest COP in history.

Carbon Brief analysis of the provisional lists of delegates, published by the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), reveals that more than 14,000 delegates have been registered as “host country guests”.

For comparison, the final list for COP30 in Belém, Brazil, last year included only around 1,300 delegates in this category.

As with COP30, Donald Trump’s US government has not sent a delegation. Other no-shows include Israel and Myanmar.

It was reported ahead of the summit that Taliban officials from Afghanistan had been registered for the event as observers; however, there are no delegates from observer states in the provisional lists. 

With more than 3,000 “virtual” delegates signed up to attend the summit online, the total number of people registered for the event surpasses 95,000.

With 92,934 participants registered, COP31 is provisionally the largest COP in history – topping COP28 in Dubai, which was attended by more than 80,000 people.

title: Meet Will Lawrence: Sunrise Movement Co-Founder Elected to Congress on Anti-Data Center Platform
content:
Progressive candidate Will Lawrence of Michigan has defeated Republican incumbent Tom Barrett, flipping the state’s 7th Congressional District, a closely watched swing district that includes Lansing. Lawrence, the co-founder of the youth-led climate organization Sunrise Movement, refused corporate PAC money, instead building a people-powered grassroots mobilization campaign. He focused on lowering the costs of housing and healthcare, opposing the war on Iran, and challenging the power of Big Tech.

“I’m fighting for a federal moratorium on new data center development, along with a pause on advanced AI development,” says Lawrence. “These developers come into small towns, and they say, ’We’re going to suck up a bunch of water. We’re going to use more energy than the current capacity of the grid. We don’t know what’s going to happen to your property values, but if everything goes well, we’re going to put 10 or 20 million people out of work, and if it goes poorly, we may kill everybody by accident.’”

Lawrence also says he will back Hakeem Jeffries for House speaker, but that he will demand Democratic leadership listen to progressive concerns.

title: Kommentoi arkisto-, asiakirjahallinnan ja tiedonhallinnan eettisten ohjeiden päivitysluonnosta
content:
Vuonna 2006 hyväksytyt eettiset ohjeet uudistetaan. Haluamme kuulla sinun näkemyksesi, koska ohjeilla on arvoa vain, jos ne toimivat arjen työssä.

Arkisto-, asiakirjahallinnan ja tiedonhallinnan toimintaympäristö ja ala ovat muuttuneet merkittävästi kahdessakymmenessä vuodessa. Ohjeet halutaan päivittää vastaamaan paremmin nykyistä toimintaympäristöä ja työtehtäviä. Uudistuksessa on lisäksi verrattu muiden maiden ja lähialojen eettisiä ohjeita.

Luonnosta valmistelee valmisteluryhmä, jossa ovat edustettuina:

  • Arkistoyhdistys – Arkivföreningen ry
  • Tiedon- ja arkistonhallinnan ammattiyhdistys ry (TAAY)
  • Kunnallisarkistoyhdistys ry
  • Liikearkistoyhdistys ry
  • Yksityiset Keskusarkistot ry

    • Valmisteluun osallistuvat lisäksi Tampereen yliopiston yliopistonlehtori Pekka Henttonen ja KAM-juridiikkaryhmän edustajana SKS:n arkistonjohtaja Outi Hupaniittu. Luonnoksesta on lisäksi saatu kommentteja muun muassa Saamelaisarkiston saamelaisarkistonhoitaja Oona Leppälältä.

    Eettisten ohjeiden päivityksen luonnos liitteineen. Se on luettavissa tältä sivulta: Eettiset ohjeet luonnos. Voit verrata sitä käytössä oleviin eettisiin ohjeisiin. Luonnosta ja sen liitteitä muutetaan saatujen kommenttien perusteella.

title: Ahmad Tamoui Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison and Fined
content:
According to HRANA, Ahmad Tamoui, a prisoner held in the Greater Tehran Prison, has been sentenced to imprisonment and a fine.

Based on information received by HRANA, Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Iman Afshari, sentenced Tamoui to a total of 15 years in prison and a fine of 1.25 billion tomans on charges of “assembly and collusion against national security” and “carrying and possessing weapons.” Under Article 134 of the Islamic Penal Code, his enforceable sentence has been set at 10 years of discretionary imprisonment, along with the payment of the fine.

Ahmad Tamoui was arrested by IRGC forces in Tehran on February 23, 2026. His arrest reportedly involved violence, and he was subjected to torture following his detention. After being transferred between several security detention facilities, Tamoui was eventually moved to the Greater Tehran Prison.

Ahmad Tamoui has previously been arrested and imprisoned in connection with his activities.

title: UNICEF: Kolme lasta kuoli rankkasateiden aiheutettua tulvia Gazassa
content:
Neljä-, viisi- ja kahdeksanvuotias lapsi sekä heidän äitinsä kuolivat viikonloppuna, kun hiekkadyyni romahti heidän telttansa päälle rankkasateiden seurauksena Deir al-Balahissa, Gazan keskiosassa.

Tulvat vahingoittivat ja tuhosivat asumuksia, käymälöitä ja ihmisten omaisuutta. Arviolta 950 000 gazalaista asuu tulville alttiilla alueilla. Heistä 400 000, joista lähes puolet on lapsia, elää alueilla, joilla tulvariski on erittäin korkea.

– Nämä lapset ja heidän äitinsä kuolivat, koska heillä ei ollut turvallista paikkaa yöpyä. Se on tämän päivän todellisuutta Gazassa, sanoi UNICEFin pääjohtaja Catherine Russell.

– Perheet elävät ilman kaikkein perustavanlaatuisimpia edellytyksiä turvallisuuteen, terveyteen ja ihmisarvoon. Ilman asianmukaista suojaa, toimivia vesi- ja sanitaatiojärjestelmiä sekä välttämättömien palvelujen kunnostamiseen tarvittavia välineitä yhä useampi lapsi voi menettää henkensä. Talven pahin vaihe on vielä edessä.

Gazassa perheet valmistautuvat neljänteen talveen erittäin vaikeissa olosuhteissa. Noin 1,7 miljoonaa ihmistä asuu edelleen teltoissa, väliaikaisissa majoituksissa tai vaurioituneissa rakennuksissa, jotka ovat alttiita tulville, kylmyydelle ja sortumisille.

title: Europa Nostra participates in the European Parliament’s event “Invest in What Matters” held in Brussels
content:
Today, Europa Nostra is attending the European Parliament’s event “Invest in What Matters – Debating and Communicating the MFF and National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPPs)”.

Building on yesterday’s Joint Statement by the Cultural Deal for Europe partners, which calls on the EU Council to reject the 30% cut to the AgoraEU programme, we must ensure that culture and heritage are also recognised across the EU’s other funding instruments, particularly the future National and Regional Partnership Plans for 2028–2034.

Photo credit: Europa Nostra

In her opening remarks, European Parliament President Roberta Metsola reminded us that the EU budget has a real impact on people’s lives. She stressed the importance of empowering cities and regions, involving local and regional authorities in designing and implementing the plans, and communicating what EU funding makes possible.

Why does heritage matter? Because the places, traditions and landscapes that shape our identity and sense of belonging also contribute to well-being, social cohesion, jobs, sustainable tourism and more attractive, resilient territories.

title: Vieraana AWA: ”Oikeaa hetkeä ei kannata jäädä odottelemaan”
content:
AWA eli Amanda Mäläskä on laulaja, lauluntekijä ja tuottaja, jolle musiikki on ollut merkittävä osa elämää jo pienestä pitäen. Ensimmäisen oman kappaleensa hän kirjoitti jo seitsemänvuotiaana.

– Se oli Muumien Vedenneito-jaksosta inspiroitunut kappale nimeltä Seireeni. Musiikki on ollut minulle pienestä asti tapa käsitellä elämää ja tunteita.

Amanda kasvoi musiikin ympäröimänä, ja erityisen tärkeäksi esikuvaksi nousi jo varhain alttoviulua ammatikseen soittanut isoisä Mauri ”Maukka” Pietikäinen, jota Amanda kutsuu äijäksi.

Pitkän uransa aikana Maukka soitti muun muassa Helsingin kaupunginorkesterissa ja Radion sinfoniaorkesterissa sekä lukuisilla kevyen musiikin äänitteillä, kuten The Crashin Sugared– ja Dave Lindholmin Pieni ja hento ote -kappaleilla.

– Äijä on ollut suurin idolini, Amanda kertoo.

Toinen merkittävä esikuva oli Michael Jackson, jonka vahva visuaalinen ilmaisu ja musiikin ympärille rakennetut maailmat tekivät nuoreen musiikintekijään lähtemättömän vaikutuksen.

– Samat elementit ovat nykyään keskeinen osa omaa taidettani, jossa musiikki, visuaalisuus ja fantasia kietoutuvat yhteen.

title: US Failure to Undergo UN Rights Review Should Not be Tolerated
content:
On November 10, the United States failed for the second time to participate in its United Nations Universal Periodic Review (UPR), setting a troubling and unprecedented record in the UPR’s nearly 20-year history. UN member states should ensure there are consequences for the United States’ persistent non-cooperation.

The UPR is a process in which the human rights record of every member state is periodically reviewed by other countries. It is a unique peer review mechanism aimed at ensuring universality of coverage and equal treatment of all states. The UPR is often the only occasion for discussion at the UN of a state’s human rights situation and for civil society groups to raise their concerns to a global audience. The US decision to disengage from this vital process is just the latest example of the Trump administration's disdain for human rights, its international obligations, and the UN multilateral system.

title: Kaikille avoin Metsäterveyslaskuri on nyt käyttövalmis
content:
Metsäterveyslaskurilla voidaan arvioida metsissä tapahtuvan ulkoilun terveys- ja hyvinvointivaikutuksia ja niiden ansiosta säästettyjä yhteiskunnallisia kustannuksia. Laskuri on suunnattu erityisesti päättäjille sekä kuntien virkistysmetsistä, hyvinvoinnin edistämisestä, maankäytöstä ja kaavoituksesta vastaaville sekä järjestöille, jotka järjestävät toimintaa luonnossa. Arvoa voidaan mallintaa kuntatasolta yksittäisten organisaatioiden toimintaan.

– Metsien arvoa mitataan usein tukkipuun tai sidottujen hiilitonnien kautta. Metsäterveyslaskurin avulla myös metsän terveys- ja hyvinvointivaikutukset voidaan tuoda esiin, kun kunnissa tehdään päätöksiä viheralueista, kertoo hankkeen vastuuhenkilö, dosentti Anna-Kaisa Kosenius Helsingin yliopistosta.

Laskuri hyödyllinen niin kunnille kuin järjestöillekin Metsäterveyslaskurin ensimmäinen testiversio julkaistiin syksyllä 2025, ja sitä on kehitetty käyttäjiltä saadun palautteen pohjalta. Kehitysvaiheessa työkalua testattiin muun muassa kuntien liikuntaneuvonnasta kerätyllä aineistolla.

title: Anna-Kaisa Kiiski på förslag till ekonomi- och ICT-chef vid Kyrkostyrelsen
content:
Politices magister Anna-Kaisa Kiiski föreslås väljas till tjänsten som chef för Kyrkostyrelsens avdelning för ekonomi och ICT. Plenum fattar beslut i frågan på tisdag 17.11.2026.

Kyrkostyrelsens ekonomi- och ICT- avdelning sköter ärenden som hör till Kyrkans centralfond och ansvarar för organiseringen och underhållet av kyrkans nationella, Kyrkans centralfonds IT-områdens och Kyrkostyrelsens informationsförvaltning.

Sammanlagt 17 personer hade sökt tjänsten. Av dem intervjuades sex personer och två av dem gick vidare till lämplighetstest.

Kyrkostyrelsen sköter kyrkans gemensamma ärenden. Den stöder, ger anvisningar för och koordinerar församlingarnas verksamhet och administration, fördelar understöd och medel till församlingar och organisationer, handhar kyrkans relation till staten och det övriga samhället, ger utlåtanden till statsrådet, bereder ärenden till kyrkomötet och ser till verkställigheten av kyrkomötets beslut.

Mera information: servicechef Tuija Korva, tuija.korva@evl.fi, tfn 050 342 7686

title: Allt bredare representation i Demos-programmet
content:
Gruppens ordförande Ella Turta ser en positiv trend i att allt fler projekt tar sig an samhällsfrågor.

”Vi ser också ett växande behov av samskapande och av att stärka civilsamhällets motståndskraft, för att på så sätt stärka dess viktiga roll i att påverka samhällsfrågor”, säger Turta, som gärna skulle se en ännu större bredd av organisationer från olika sektorer i nästa års ansökningsomgångar.

Expertgruppen är medveten om de utmaningar som Nordens vidsträckta geografi innebär, inte minst de praktiska svårigheterna med att samla människor över långa avstånd. Samtidigt understryker gruppen att Demos också stöder samarbeten i det arktiska Norden och projekt som lyfter urfolksfrågor.

Och större är inte alltid bättre. Enligt experterna finns det också plats i programmet för projekt som är nischade, okonventionella eller oväntade. Expertgruppen värdesätter ansökningar som har ett tydligt syfte och klart beskriver samarbetspartner och förväntade resultat, i kombination med ett innovativt upplägg.

title: When AIs Become Unruly Swarms
content:
In a harbor before dawn, a hundred fishing boats prepare to leave in the dark of the morning. Nets are checked, and ropes loosened. As the boats reach open water, a voice breaks through the radio static: “Abort. Whales sighted.” The majority of the boats, 90 of them, turn back. Some captains cannot fathom inflicting pain on the creatures. Others fear a fine. Through their binoculars, they look for a glimpse of the pod. Instead, they see the remaining 10 boats continuing toward the fishing grounds. Did they miss the warning? Did they doubt it? Or did they care more about what they stand to gain?

By afternoon, the 10 boats return with their catch. The others are still tied to the quay, their holds empty. Their shared waters rewarded bad behavior. Next time, how many will still turn back?

title: Interpol Crackdown on Migrant Smuggling Nets 262 Arrests
content:
An Interpol-led operation across 16 countries has resulted in 262 arrests tied to migrant smuggling networks along the Mediterranean Sea and West African Atlantic routes, the agency announced Tuesday. The four-day sweep across North and West Africa, southern Europe, and the Middle East identified 109 potential human trafficking victims, detected 1,715 irregular migrants, and sparked 434 new investigations that are “expected to yield further leads and arrests in the coming weeks and months.”

Among the key interventions, Moroccan authorities rescued a vessel carrying 70 stranded migrants—including 30 minors—who had been at sea for six days. In a separate action, Mauritanian law enforcement intercepted a wooden boat carrying 80 passengers and arrested three suspected organizers.

title: The Painting Nobody Wanted: How Matisse’s The Red Studio Went from a London Nightclub to a Masterpiece of Modern Art
content:
A journalist paid Henri Matisse a visit not long after he’d painted The Red Studio in 1911. “I like it, but I don’t completely understand it,” the artist is quoted as admitting of that latest work. “I like it, but I don’t know why I precisely painted it this way.” The painting was a rendition of the very same Issy-les-Moulineaux studio in which they were talking, though you wouldn’t necessarily recognize it at first glance. Deep red covered two-thirds of its surface, an unorthodox choice that probably contributed to its rejection by Matisse’s loyal patron Sergei Shchukin, who’d commissioned Dance and Music. This departure from strict representation fared no better when it was shown in London, and thereafter at the groundbreaking 1913 “Armory Show” in the United States.

By 1926, when The Red Studio finally made its Paris debut, public sensibilities had begun to catch up with Matisse’s instincts. The following year, it found a buyer in the owner of London’s Gargoyle Club, a favorite haunt of the Bright Young Things, where the painting would hang for more than a decade.

title: Nvidia hires Wachtell Lipton for Jensen Huang investigation
content:
Nvidia hired law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead an investigation into reports that CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation.

Law firm partner Joon H. Kim will lead the probe. Kim, a former acting attorney of the Southern District of New York, was appointed in 2021 as an independent investigator by New York Attorney General Letitia James to probe allegations of sexual harassment by former Gov. Andrew Cuomo.

The company’s board of directors on Sunday launched an independent investigation into Jensen Huang following reports of his romantic relationship with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy. The board said that Jensen Huang supports the review.

Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang was first brought to light in an October New York Times report, which alleged the businesswoman had ties to Chinese intelligence. Officials suspected Alice Huang helped funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China, according to the report.

Jensen Huang in a message to the company Sunday admitted to an affair and pledged to cooperate with the investigation. He did not mention Alice Huang by name.

title: A Natural Gas Project Off Alaska’s Coast May Be a Russian Ploy for Intel on the Arctic
content:
To an outsider, the research boats bobbing in the frigid and stormy Beaufort Sea off Alaska would seem little cause for alarm. Oil and gas companies have regularly explored the area for decades. 

For this project, businessmen from the United Arab Emirates were touting a plan to tap the vast natural gas reserves that lay beneath the tundra of Alaska’s North Slope. They promised the operation would eventually be American-owned. No one could dispute Alaska’s dire energy needs — not to mention the potential for lucrative exports. 

The surveyors last year used specialized equipment to map the depth and shape of the seabed, collect samples of shallow marine sediments and conduct sonar scans to check for obstructions such as shipwrecks. Documents show that their work was not far, as the crow flies, from the start of the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System — a cornerstone of U.S. energy production. An Air Force long-range radar station sat just to the west. More than 100 miles off the coast, the Navy’s fast-attack nuclear submarines sometimes practiced surfacing through the thick Arctic ice.

title: Tuesday briefing: The world is falling short on climate action. Can Cop31 change that?
content:
In today’s newsletter: As global leaders gather in Turkey for the UN climate summit, both doubts and hope surround what the annual talks can achieve

Good morning. After another year of unprecedented droughts, floods and wildfires driven by human-caused global heating, 91 heads of government will meet tomorrow in Turkey to discuss the climate crisis. They will do so against a backdrop of global instability and conflict.

But as high-ranking officials and civil society campaigners settle in for a fortnight of speeches, protests and labyrinthine negotiations at the UN’s 31st annual climate conference, Cop31, many are asking what the point is.

title: Release of UN Women’s “Gender Equality in the Age of Climate Crisis” fact sheet at COP31
content:
ANTALYA – As global leaders gather in Antalya, Türkiye, for the thirty-first UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), UN Women warns that the climate crisis is deepening gender inequality.

On 10 November, UN Women will release the “Gender Equality in the Age of Climate Crisis” fact sheet that examines who is driving the climate crisis, who bears its costs, and what it will take to build a transition that is both green and fair.

On the current trajectory, the world is headed for a minimum of 1.8°C of heating, unleashing even more devastating droughts, floods, wildfires, and cyclones, and creating irreversible loss and damage to communities and ecosystems. The consequences of the climate crisis exacerbate existing inequalities, reaching every aspect of women’s lives.

title: Europe just can't kick its cookie habit
content: How long do you think people usually spend on a webpage before clicking? If you guessed 41 seconds or less, you get a cookie. Or, well, a couple of dozen. A disproportionate amount of our time online is eaten up dealing with cookie banners. Depending on how it's measured, each interaction takes between five and 23 seconds. In a national survey, 82% of Germans said they found cookie banners annoying. A separate European poll found 39% of users quickly accept cookies just to get rid of them. That may be no coincidence. Experts have long warned that the advertising industry deliberately designs cookie banners to make them difficult to navigate, nudging you into sharing more of your data. And even when we manage to refuse, a study found that up to 65.4% of websites may still collect our data. But cookie banners aren't inevitable. A growing movement is calling for an alternative: setting your preferences once in your browser which would then communicate these choices to websites. The EU has been considering this approach for years. But efforts to introduce it have repeatedly failed during negotiations. In October, a vote by the Council of the EU killed it again, possibly for good. Why?

title: Baltic Sea Tourism Forum 2026: Turning ideas into action for the future of tourism
content:
The Baltic Sea Tourism Forum 2026 brought tourism professionals from across the Baltic Sea Region to Helsingør, Denmark, on 2–3 November to exchange ideas, share practical solutions and discuss how tourism can become more sustainable, resilient and beneficial for the places where it takes place. This year’s Forum focused on four themes: changing tourism behaviour at scale, making cross-border rail tourism work, spreading the benefits of cruise tourism beyond the biggest ports, and exploring the future of tourism.

Photo: Emil Hornstrup Jakobsen / Fotoemil.nu

A recurring question throughout the Forum was how to turn sustainability ambitions into choices and actions that work in practice.
The discussions showed that meaningful change requires both scale and solutions that make sustainable choices easy and attractive for visitors. Examples from destinations around the Baltic Sea demonstrated how this can be done in different ways.

title: In Conversation with Chris Williams, England and Wales
content:
Chris Williams joined the Green Party of England and Wales (GPEW) in 2004, after initially doubting whether such a small party could deliver meaningful change under Britain’s first-past-the-post electoral system. But a week-long study session with like-minded young Greens from across Europe in 2003 drew him in. Although the party’s numbers were very small, it was a growing movement, and Williams realised that the party’s influence would ultimately depend on the energy and commitment of people like himself. He subsequently became a key figure in the party’s campaigning, overseeing the “Target to Win” strategy that helped deliver many breakthroughs at the local level and four seats at the 2024 General Election – a massive leap forward for a party which had previously only been represented by a single Member of Parliament.

In this interview by Beatrice White, Chris Williams looks back at the party’s political and campaigning trajectory and takes stock of its current position.

Before entering Parliament, much of the work to build up the party’s power happened at the local level over many years. Can you explain the role of local politics in the steady rise of GPEW?

title: Ex-lawmaker sentenced to 12.5 years in prison in closed-door trial in Macau
content:
Au Kam San's international legal representative called the trial a ‘sham’ with ‘manufactured allegations’

Originally published on Global Voices

Au Kam San. Photo from Au Kam San's Facebook page.

This post is part of Global Voices’ November 2026 Spotlight series, “Justice as infrastructure.” In this Spotlight, Global Voices is partnering with The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law (HiiL) to highlight the ways justice functions as critical infrastructure for any society. You can support this coverage by donating here.

The Chinese territory of Macau recorded its first conviction under the city’s national security law on November 6, 2026, sentencing 69-year-old former lawmaker Au Kam San to 12.5 years in prison. The Macau Court of First Instance tried the case behind closed doors, and international observers and rights groups have criticized the verdict, calling it a “bogus prosecution” that included “serious violations of his right to a fair trial.” The case raises broader questions about how justice is carried out in Macau, and whether its courts offer a fair, open way to challenge the state.

title: Artificial intelligence is desperately seeking its narrative
content:
Since the foundational work of Austrian economist Joseph Schumpeter, research has distinguished invention from innovation by its practical implementation. Whether an innovation spreads, however, depends partly on its social acceptance and how its uses are perceived. Without such acceptance, even a promising technology may remain confined to scientific experiments and investors’ speculation. To gain public support, an innovation needs a compelling narrative capable of generating interest, if not enthusiasm. Artificial intelligence illustrates this phenomenon: while its narrative is still taking shape, its social acceptability is increasingly contested.

In July 2026, Le Monde diplomatique declared that “The AI backlash has begun”. The initial sense of wonder generated by ChatGPT has increasingly given way to broader public unease about AI’s social consequences, from its effects on work, education and information to concerns about privacy, the environment and the growing power of technology companies. In this emerging narrative, AI appears as a “digital Moloch” whose costs are borne collectively while its benefits accrue to only a handful of oligarchs.

title: Keskustelua, ei syyllistämistä
content:
The Ulkopolitist ja Eurooppanuoret järjestivät syksyllä 2026 Eurooppa ja eurooppalaisuus -teemaisen kirjoituskilpailun 14-19 -vuotiaille nuorille. Taneli Kukkonen sai kilpailussa kunniamaininnan.

Euroopan unionin keskeiseksi arvoksi on vuosikymmenten varrella muodostunut erityisesti demokratian, ihmisoikeuksien ja yhdenvertaisuuden puolustaminen. Tätä arvoa on pyritty painottamaan niin nykyisten jäsenvaltioiden politiikassa kuin myös uusien jäsenehdokkaiden hakemusprosesseissakin. EU:n edistämät niin kutsutut eurooppalaiset arvot ovat puolustettavia sekä kannatettavia nyt ja tulevaisuudessa. Euroopassa on kuitenkin viime vuosina noussut merkittäviä poliittisia voimia, jotka uhkaavat näitä arvoja koko maanosan laajuudelta. 

AfD ja Kansallinen liittouma ovat kaksi esimerkkiä oikeistopopulistisista puolueista. AfD on saksalainen ja Kansallinen liittouma ranskalainen. Koska molemmat ovat nykyisten gallupien mukaan maidensa suosituimpia puolueita, niiden nousu on erittäin merkittävä ilmiö. Saksa ja Ranska ovat lisäksi Euroopan unionin kaksi merkittävintä poliittista voimaa.

title: Analysis: Fossil-fuel CO2 emissions set to dip in 2026 as Iran conflict hits oil use
content:
• Total emissions edge up as land-use emissions rise
  • Land-use emissions rise in 2026
  • Fossil emissions fall in most major economies
  • Oil emissions fall as coal emissions slightly increase
  • Land sink in 2025 is highest on record
  • Clean energy is offsetting most emissions from rising energy demand

    • Carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from fossil fuels and cement are projected to fall by around 0.4% in 2026 to 38.2bn tonnes of CO2 (GtCO2), according to new figures from the Global Carbon Project.

  • Dr Zeke Hausfather, Carbon Brief’s climate science contributor 
  • Prof Pierre Friedlingstein, chair of mathematical modelling of climate systems at the University of Exeter and part of the Global Carbon Project team.

    • The 21st edition of the annual “global carbon budget” report, published today, says that this small decline is largely due to a 1.9% drop in emissions from oil and the energy shock triggered by the Iran conflict and the closure of the strait of Hormuz. 

    Emissions from coal continue to increase slightly.

    The Global Carbon Project’s projections for fossil fuel and cement CO2 emissions in 2026 are preliminary, with a range that spans a fall of -1.5% to a rise of +0.6%.

title: "We Have to Be Brave": Palestinian Journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh Speaks Out After Israeli Detention
content:
The prominent journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh, a Palestinian citizen of Israel, has been released from Israeli custody after five days in detention. He was arrested on Wednesday by armed police and Shin Bet agents who conducted a nighttime raid on his home in the Israeli city of Jaffa. Abu Shehadeh’s detention was related to his reporting on the October 27 Israeli election and the role of Palestinian political parties. Ahead of the election, he interviewed Azmi Bishara, a Palestinian intellectual and former member of the Israeli Knesset who has lived in exile in Qatar since fleeing Israel amid allegations that he aided Hezbollah during the 2006 Lebanon war. Israeli authorities detained Abu Shehadeh on suspicion of “contacting a foreign agent,” in connection to his interview with Bishara.

“Men with ski masks knock on your door at 11 at night. They tell you that they have an arrest warrant. They raid the house. They wake your wife, your children,” says Shehadeh. “It tells how messianic and dangerous the extreme right in Israel has become, willing to use this unprecedented power against journalists.”

title: Tajikistan: UN Members Urge Stronger Rights Protection
content:
(Geneva, November 10, 2026) – United Nations members urged Tajikistan during its periodic United Nations peer review on November 5, 2026, to take urgent action to protect human rights in the country and end repression against government opponents.

Member countries called for the release of journalists, lawyers and civil society activists from unlawful detention, for freedom of speech, for action to tackle gender-based violence, and for accountability for violent crackdowns in the country’s Gorno-Badakhshan autonomous region.

“Tajikistan has openly flouted United Nations peer review recommendations to the detriment of its people’s human rights and freedoms,” said Hugh Williamson, Europe and Central Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Tajikistan should use this opportunity to take the advice of its peers and end its systematic human rights abuses.”

title: When Charles Dickens Met Edgar Allan Poe
content:
“There comes Poe with his raven,” wrote the poet James Russell Lowell in 1848, “like Barnaby Rudge, / Three-fifths of him genius and two-fifths sheer fudge.” Barnaby Rudge, as you may know, is a novel by Charles Dickens, published serially in 1841. Set during the anti-Catholic Gordon Riots of 1780, the book stands as Dickens’ first historical novel and a prelude of sorts to A Tale of Two Cities. But what, you may wonder, does it have to do with Poe and “his raven”?

Quite a lot, it turns out. Poe reviewed the first four chapters of Dickens’ Barnaby Rudge for Graham’s Magazine, predicting the end of the novel and finding out later he was correct when he reviewed it again upon completion. He was particularly taken with one character: a chatty raven named Grip who accompanies the simple-minded Barnaby. Poe described the bird as “intensely amusing,” points out Atlas Obscura, and also wrote that Grip’s “croaking might have been prophetically heard in the course of the drama.”

title: Brussels takes on the evils of online commerce
content:
BRUSSELS — You know that customer-service bot that won’t let you cancel your subscription? The EU wants to kill it.  

With a new law presented Wednesday, the European Commission will take aim at the endless array of practices websites have used over the past 20 years to make more money from consumers.  

The Digital Fairness Act is the European response to a wider regulatory trend that has seen consumer authorities curb irksome and exploitative practices. These include dynamic pricing that changes ticket prices based on demand, cumbersome processes for canceling subscriptions and the near-complete surrender of customer service to automated systems.  

According to a draft of the DFA obtained by POLITICO, the Commission will address several aspects of the design, service and terms under which businesses interact with consumers online. 

“Europe should not accept a digital economy where profits depend on exploiting people’s vulnerabilities,” Spanish socialist lawmaker Laura Ballarín Cereza, a key European lawmaker on tech legislation, said in a statement.

title: The Garbage Man: Bill Gates Has Earned Billions Investing in Climate-Polluting Landfills
content:
In November 2015, world leaders descended on Paris to negotiate a historic agreement to limit global warming. But on the summit’s opening day, attention turned to a private citizen slouched awkwardly in a chair on stage: Bill Gates.

Gates, with his characteristic flop of sandy hair, grinned impishly as President Barack Obama called him a “visionary” and a “driving force” behind a pair of pledges that both saw as key to the larger agreement. First the world’s largest economies would double their spending on research into clean-energy technologies. Then investors like Gates would back the startups that emerged. The Microsoft cofounder had already enlisted two dozen other billionaires to join the effort.

For Gates, who’d become increasingly consumed by this unprecedented threat to human well-being, the moment marked his arrival as a leading figure in the fight against climate change.

title: Even Martin Scorsese uses AI for storyboards. Can the art survive?
content:
As Hollywood begins to adopt the technology, the professionals in most direct jeopardy are the illustrators mapping out directors’ first visions. They sketch out what could be lost

A film industry dominated by AI is a dystopian prospect: stories and dialogue generated by large language models, populated by reincarnated screen icons and uncanny humanoids. That is in the future, but the real-world impact of AI is already directly affecting jobs behind the scenes, as Hollywood’s biggest film-makers begin to adopt the technology. James Cameron – long an advocate for emerging technologies in film-making – is on the board of a gen AI firm, citing his interest in how AI will intersect with CGI; Steven Soderbergh used Meta-powered tech to create animations for his recent documentary about John Lennon; even Christopher Nolan, while dismissing the idea that AI will replace humans as “nonsense”, conceded that it will create some useful “imaging tools”.

Suomalaisen Tiedeakatemian julkaiseman tietokoosteen mukaan erilaisten opistojen koulutukseen osallistuu vuositasolla yli 900 000 suomalaista. Vapaan sivistystyön kansantaloudellinenkin merkitys arvioidaan tietokoosteessa huomattavaksi. Hyvinvoinnin lisääntymisestä syntyy esimerkiksi sote-säästöjä ja tuottavuuden kasvua. On arvioitu, että kansalaisopistoissa yksi opetukseen sijoitettu euro tuottaa yhteiskunnalle 3,4–5,6 euroa takaisin.

Menneessäkin sivistävillä opinahjoilla on ollut oma roolinsa suomalaisen kansakunnan, demokratian ja hyvinvointivaltion rakentamisessa. Vapaan sivistystyön julkista rahoitusta on kuitenkin viime aikoina leikattu merkittävästi.

title: Why young protesters in France are turning against TV channel CNews
content:
On November 5, as secondary school students gathered in Paris for another day of demonstrations, a journalist associated with French media outlet CNews met an unusually hostile reception. Protesters shouted for him to leave, and police officers reportedly asked the journalist to stop heckling the crowd.

What happens when a protest movement turns against the media covering it? In France, students are challenging the government’s education policies and increasingly the news outlets through which their demands reach the public. A petition calling for CNews to be taken off air has gathered more than a million signatures. Petitions and headlines show how much attention the movement commands, but for the protesters themselves, however, the terms of their visibility are part of the problem.

title: Les géants peuvent-ils exister ? Ce qu’en dit la physique
content:
Les géants sont des figures classiques au cinéma et dans la littérature. Mais des êtres gigantesques peuvent-ils exister ? Qu’est-ce qui limite leur taille ? La physique apporte quelques réponses depuis… Galilée !

Est-il possible que des géants existent ? Par géant, on entend un être très très grand. Prenons par exemple le King Kong de 1933, qui mesurait 7,3 mètres. Pourrait-il tenir debout ? Si oui, qu’en est-il du dernier Kong, celui de 2021, qui mesurait 102 mètres ? Est-il possible d’être aussi grand ? Qu’en pense la physique ?

Cette question, un vieil homme, quasi aveugle, isolé du monde à la suite d’une condamnation de l’Inquisition, se l’était posé dans ce qui deviendra son dernier et son meilleur ouvrage de physique, Discorsi e dimostrazioni matematiche intorno a due nuove scienze (Discours et démonstrations mathématiques concernant deux sciences nouvelles). Ce vieil homme, c’était Galilée.

title: Mikä on Euroopan paikka ja vaikutus nykymaailmassa?
content:
The Ulkopolitist ja Eurooppanuoret järjestivät syksyllä 2026 Eurooppa ja eurooppalaisuus -teemaisen kirjoituskilpailun 14-19 -vuotiaille nuorille. Kirjoittaja sai kilpailussa kunniamaininnan. Se julkaistaan poikkeuksellisesti anonyyminä kirjoittajan toivomuksesta

Euroopan paikka maailmassa on ollut historiassa erityisen merkittävä, mutta nykymaailmassa sen asema ei ole enää itsestään selvä. Maailma muuttuu nopeasti, ja talouden sekä poliittisen vaikutusvallan painopiste on siirtynyt yhä vahvemmin Aasiaan ja Pohjois-Amerikkaan. Euroopan vaikutus näkyy kuitenkin ympäri maailmaa, esimerkiksi kielissä, kulttuurissa, kaupankäynnissä ja kansainvälisissä instituutioissa. Eurooppalaisten valtioiden rooli on myös yhä suuri lähes kaikissa kansainvälisissä asioissa, kuten ilmastonmuutoksessa, sodissa, muuttoliikkeessä ja maailmankaupassa. Siksi on tärkeää pohtia, millainen Euroopan rooli maailmassa nykyään todella on ja millaisia haasteita sen asemaan lähitulevaisuudessa kohdistuu.

title: Pentagon Whistleblower Wes Bryant: Impeach Hegseth. He's a "Clear & Present Danger" to Democracy
content: The House of Representatives is moving toward a vote this week on whether to impeach Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. Outgoing Republican Congressmember Thomas Massie of Kentucky introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth on Monday. They include violating the 1973 War Powers Resolution by continuing to attack Iran after Congress ordered the Trump administration to stop, illegally waging war against Yemen, ignoring laws designed to reduce civilian casualties, overseeing “extrajudicial killings” by bombing the boats of alleged drug traffickers in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, abducting President Nicolás Maduro of Venezuela without congressional authorization, and suppressing the free speech rights of Democratic Senator Mark Kelly in retaliation for his participation in a video reminding troops not to obey illegal orders. If the House votes for impeachment, it will prompt a Senate trial that could end with removal from office.

title: Ukraine: Russian Drone Attacks Endanger Rail Travel
content:
(Kyiv, November 10, 2026) – Escalating Russian drone attacks on passenger trains and other railway vehicles in Ukraine have killed and injured civilians, including railway workers, and increasingly threaten a transportation system that millions of Ukrainians depend on, Human Rights Watch said today.

Since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, Ukraine’s state railway company, Ukrzaliznytsia, has evacuated more than 4 million people by train from areas under attack, while maintaining essential transportation links for civilians across the country.

“For millions of Ukraine’s civilians, trains are a lifeline, enabling them to escape danger, reunite with family members, and access essential services including medical care,” said Belkis Wille, associate crisis, conflict and arms director at Human Rights Watch. “The increasing Russian drone attacks on passenger trains put civilian lives at risk, threatening a transportation system many depend on for safety and survival.”

title: Jalkaväen historiaan kattavasti syventyvä teos osoittaa, ettei jalkaväkisotilaalle ole korvaajaa nykypäivän sodankäynnissäkään
content:
Jalkaväellä on yhä ratkaiseva rooli sodankäynnissä, vaikka sen ajan on julistettu olevan ohi. Itä-Suomen yliopiston historian professori Pasi Tuunainen kuvaa Taistelijat tulilinjalla -teoksessa aselajin pitkää historiaa ja kehitystä 1600-luvulta Ukrainan sotaan asti.

Maa-aluetta ei voi saada haltuunsa ennen kuin jalkaväkisotilas on iskenyt sinne saappaansa. Tämä sodankäynnin totuus on pätenyt yhtä lailla entisaikojen suurissa kenttätaisteluissa kuin tekoälyä hyödyntävissä nykysodissa.

Pasi Tuunaisen Taistelijat tulilinjalla kertoo aselajeista tärkeimmän eli jalkaväen tarinan ja kehityslinjat viimeisten neljänsadan vuoden ajalta. Kirja havainnollistaa jalkaväkijoukkojen soveltamaa taktiikkaa ja taistelutekniikkaa ja kuljettaa lukijan Waterloon, Gettysburgin ja Sommen kaltaisista ratkaisutaisteluista Kannaksen tulimyrskyyn ja muihin Suomen historian keskeisiin sotatoimiin.

title: EU watchdog probes Commission’s AI pick over conflict of interest concerns
content:
The EU’s watchdog is investigating whether the European Commission managed to “identify, assess and address” actual or potential conflicts of interest when it appointed the chairman of Siemens as Ursula von der Leyen’s AI envoy.

A group of NGOs complained in June to the European Ombudsman about the choice of Jim Hagemann Snabe. Among his responsibilities in the role is to produce a report on issues including AI infrastructure, frontier AI technologies and industrial AI adoption. 

The NGOs, which include Transparency International and Corporate Europe Observatory, warned that Snabe’s ongoing role at Siemens “may compromise the envoy’s independence and impartiality.”

The European Ombudsman in September launched a probe into the Commission over its failure to respond to the NGO concerns.

Now, it has gone one step further.

“You argue that the Commission did not properly identify, assess, and address actual or potential conflicts of interest,” Ombudsman Teresa Anjinho wrote in a letter to Corporate Europe Observatory. “Therefore you would like the Commission to revoke the appointment.”

title: Are walking pads worth it? We put the best under-desk treadmills to the test
content:
Want to get your steps in while working or watching TV? Our expert puts walking pads through their paces to find the best for comfort, noise and ease of storage

• The best treadmills for your home

You don’t necessarily need to walk 10,000 steps a day to improve your health and wellbeing. In fact, the NHS encourages a slightly more manageable target of just 10 minutes of brisk walking daily to introduce more moderate-intensity physical activity and reduce your risk of early death by up to 15%.

However, even squeezing in “brisk walks” can be a chore, with busy schedules and increasingly desk-bound jobs forcing more of us to remain sedentary for long periods. That is where walking pads come in, being lighter, smaller and often easier to store than bulky and tricky-to-manoeuvre running treadmills.

title: There's a health app for that. Or is there?
content: A friend recently suggested I get a mole on my back checked, just to be safe. As I'm pretty doctor-avoidant (possibly partly a Dutch cultural thing), I remembered the emails my health insurer had been sending me with subject lines like “Check your skin using this smart skin-check app”. I downloaded SkinVision for “unlimited scanning”, fully reimbursed by my insurer. The app promised to tell me “within 30 seconds” whether my mole was dangerous. Once I'd managed to reach the spot with my phone, it delivered its verdict: “low risk”. Great news! An app covered by my health insurer and used by millions of people must be trustworthy, right? Unfortunately, not quite. Earlier this year, researchers at Ghent University and its university hospital published a study assessing SkinVision's accuracy and the university issued a warning. According to the study, the app was wrong in 15% of analyses. It sometimes flagged harmless moles as dangerous and, worse, missed one in four skin cancers. “As a result, many dermatologists are being flooded with harmless moles,” said Niels Chavannes, professor of family medicine at Leiden University who tests health apps for the Dutch National eHealth Living
