title: Teddy Roosevelt’s “Bullet” Speech
content:
-This story was written with Elaina Finkelstein, a public affairs specialist in the Office of Communications.

Teddy Roosevelt was a sturdy sort, and nothing as trifling as a wee bullet wound was going to stop him from giving a speech.

Roosevelt was shot in the chest on Oct. 14, 1912, while running for reelection to the White House. He was leaving the Hotel Gilpatrick in Milwaukee, on his way to the city’s auditorium for a campaign speech.  There was a crowd, and as he was about to step into his automobile, a mentally unstable man named John Schrank pulled out a .38 Colt revolver and shot him at close range.

The bullet, according to the Theodore Roosevelt Center, “passed through a folded copy of his lengthy address, his glasses case, and his heavy winter coat. The bullet broke his fourth rib and lodged near his right lung. Doctors determined that the bullet should not be removed.”

Roosevelt, 53 and famously adventurous, scarcely seemed to mind. He stopped the crowd from assaulting Schrank, then went to the auditorium and spoke — for more than an hour.

title: Digital Commons Policy Summit 2026: for a Competitive Europe
content:
Policymakers, researchers and commoners will meet in Brussels on 12 November to shape the next phase of Europe’s Digital Commons

The NGI Commons project has announced the full programme and speaker line-up for the Digital Commons Policy Summit 2026: Digital Commons and the Open Internet Stack for a Competitive Europe. The Summit will take place on Thursday 12 November 2026 at TownHall Europe in Brussels and will also be streamed online.

The Summit brings together policymakers, researchers, industry, civil society and the communities who build and maintain the Digital Commons. Together they will discuss how Europe can make open, community-governed digital infrastructure a pillar of its tech sovereignty agenda and of upcoming initiatives for sustainable European digital infrastructures.

A final event, and a look ahead

The Summit is also the final event of NGI Commons, a Coordination and Support Action that started in January 2024 and runs until February 2027. Over three years, the project’s four partners have worked to strengthen the Digital Commons and European digital infrastructures. At the Summit, they will set out their ambitions for what comes next.

title: Commons Stories: Part 3
content:
The commons is a way of structuring relationships to our resources. Instead of a property mindset, where the only question is: does someone own it? The questions in a commons are: how do we ensure this resource can be shared by all of us? What is our mutual commitment? 

Too often, I think the commons has become shorthand for “no one owns it, so no rules apply.” That is not a commons, it is a free-for-all. And in a way, it is the mirror image of the property focus of copyright maximalism because it begins and ends with whether or not the resources are or can be private property. 

It is utterly idealistic to believe that we can have spaces with shared rules, where everyone who partakes commits to the common good. Right now, on the public web, it feels like an aspiration more than a reality. It is an open question whether the internet will evolve to support and sustain public spaces that truly operate like a commons, where everyone who contributes has some say, and everyone who benefits plays by the rules. 

It is an aspiration worth fighting for. 

Next, we’ll explore the commons as resistance and the relationships that help it thrive in the final two installments of Commons Stories.

title: Czech-Polish Dialogue Forum: A Fragmented Defence Industry, Dependence on Washington, and the War Europe Refuses to Call by Its Name
content:
The continent has capable armed forces, excellent engineers, and innovative companies, yet struggles to bring these resources together into a coherent force. The answer, they argued, lies not in another round of political declarations, but in concrete procurement orders, joint projects, and political agreement on priorities. Whether Europe can achieve any of these things remains an open question.

The problem was most forcefully articulated by Jan Farský, a Member of the European Parliament and the European People’s Party’s rapporteur on the AGILE programme. “Europe is not weak. It is just fragmented,” he said. The continent, he argued, was losing its potential through national disputes, despite possessing capable armed forces, excellent engineers, and innovative companies. European countries continued to plan, purchase, and manufacture largely along national lines and outside the EU framework.

title: Gay sheep don't come cheap
content: “That one flehmened. He wants sex,” farmer Michael Stücke says, pointing to a ram (a male sheep) tilting its head up and curling its upper lip back. This way of smelling the air is known as the flehmen response, which male animals often do before mating. We’re standing in a pasture on Stücke’s sheep farm in the German town of Löhne in North Rhine-Westphalia, observing what looks like a regular flock of sheep. In reality, it may be the world’s most famous: 36 sheep, but they’re all rams, and they’re all gay. Rams that show no interest in mating with ewes (female sheep) and instead pursue other rams are relatively useless to breeders, Stücke says, so they’re usually sent to slaughter. That is, until 2023, when advertising agency Serviceplan started buying them up at auctions and giving them a permanent home on Stücke’s farm, himself a gay farmer. A friend of his working at the agency was sad to hear about what happens to gay rams, and knew he was active in an association for gay farmers. Upptäck Finlands vackraste böcker 2025 i Finlandsinstitutets bibliotek!

Sedan 1947 har Finlands bokkonstkommitté valt ut samlingen Årets vackraste böcker, som visas på vandringsutställningar i Finland och runt om i Europa Till årets vackraste bok 2025 utsågs Erkka Filanders monumentala diktsamling Siemenholvi, som imponerade på juryn med sin formmässigt gränsöverskridande gestaltning.

Till samlingen De vackraste böckerna 2025 valdes sammanlagt 25 verk i sju olika kategorier: skönlitteratur, fack- och läroböcker, konst- och fotoböcker, barn- och ungdomsböcker, serieböcker, experimentella småtryck samt bokomslag.

Kommittén för Finlands bokkonst utser årligen en kollektion av årets vackraste böcker, en tradition sedan 1947. Syftet är att öka uppskattningen för boken som ett bokkonstnärligt helhetsverk. När kommittén väljer årets vackraste böcker söker den verk där form och innehåll samspelar och stärker varandra.

title: Gesetzentwurf: Dobrindt startet neuen Angriff aufs IFG
content:
Bei der Abschaffung des Informationsfreiheitsgesetzes kommt die Bundesregierung nicht voran. Deswegen versucht das Innenministerium es auf einem anderen Weg – versteckt in einem anderen Gesetz.

Alles spricht gegen den Plan von Alexander Dobrindt. Seit Monaten versucht der Bundesinnenminister, das Informationsfreiheitsgesetz (IFG) abzuschaffen. Doch die SPD-Fraktion will sein Vorhaben nicht mittragen, der öffentliche Widerstand ist massiv und Dobrindt kann keinen einzigen Beleg dafür vorweisen, dass das Gesetz reformiert werden müsste. 

Aber der CSU-Politiker versucht es weiter. Ein jetzt bekannt gewordener Gesetzentwurf aus Dobrindts Ministerium zeigt: das IFG soll weiterhin entkernt werden. Doch weil die geplante IFG-Reform selbst zu viel Öffentlichkeit erfahren hat, versucht Dobrindt jetzt offenbar auf anderem Weg, die Transparenz anzugreifen. Die wichtige Änderung soll in einem anderen Gesetzentwurf zu kritischer Infrastruktur versteckt werden. Geplant ist eine riesige Transparenz-Ausnahme, durch die in Zukunft eine unüberschaubar große Anzahl IFG-Anfragen abgelehnt werden könnten. Wir veröffentlichen den bisher unbekannten Gesetzentwurf.

title: Government lawyers’ lies and stonewalling endanger press freedom
content:
Government lawyers during President Donald Trump’s second term have outright lied to federal judges and refused to comply with court orders in numerous cases involving journalists and the First Amendment.

That’s according to a newly updated report from nonpartisan law and policy journal Just Security. Since last year, the journal has been evaluating the state of the “presumption of regularity” — a legal doctrine under which judges assume that the executive branch of the U.S. government is following appropriate procedures and being honest about the reasons for its actions.

That presumption was probably never warranted — after all, many of the dishonest lawyers serving in the Trump administration aren’t newcomers to the federal government. Some have been around for decades. But Just Security’s report reveals that the presumption has been consistently and shockingly undermined since Trump returned to office — leading one judge to announce that the presumption had been “destroyed.”

Judges in press freedom cases should be presuming that any claims from the administration must be heavily scrutinized.

title: Hong Kong: Human Rights Organizations Condemn Unjust Sentencing of Joshua Wong
content:
We, the undersigned organizations, condemn the November 5th sentencing of Hong Kong prodemocracy advocate Joshua Wong to a 10-year sentence by the Hong Kong High Court. This is the second time he has been sentenced under the Beijing-imposed National Security Law (NSL), which has contributed to the rapid deterioration of basic freedoms in Hong Kong.

Joshua, who marked his 30th birthday in prison three weeks ago, rose to prominence as a teenager as the cofounder of the student group Scholarism, which opposed the introduction of pro-Beijing propaganda into Hong Kong's schools. He helped lead the historic 2014 Umbrella Movement and in 2016 created the prodemocracy Demosistō party, which was forced to disband after the approval of the NSL in 2020. He has received international acclaim for his democratic activism, including multiple nominations for the Nobel Peace Prize.

title: HER – Å forelske seg i KI
content:
Filmvisning og samtale på Vega Scene, onsdag 2. desember kl. 17.30

Samtale med filmskaper Tonje Hessen Schei, psykolog og forfatter Sissel Gran og professor Petter Bae Brandtzæg, ledet av Tellef Raabe, prosjektleder i Fritt Ord.

Theodore lever av å skrive inderlige brev på vegne av folk som ikke klarer det selv. Så forelsker han seg i operativsystemet sitt. Da regissør Spike Jonzes moderne klassiker Her kom i 2013, var denne ideen science fiction. I dag har millioner av mennesker daglige samtaler med KI-assistenter som husker hva de har fortalt, svarer med varm stemme og alltid har tid.

Her, med Joaquin Phoenix i hovedrollen og Scarlett Johansson som stemmen til Samantha, vant Oscar og Golden Globe for beste originalmanus. Filmen står igjen som kanskje den mest presise skildringen av hva som skjer når teknologien flytter inn i det mest private. Og virkeligheten imiterer fiksjonen: Da OpenAI lanserte sin taleassistent i 2024, la toppsjef Sam Altman ut ett ord på X: «her». Stemmen hørtes ut som Johanssons.

title: What comes after networked authoritarianism?
content:
October’s Spotlight contributors illuminated a range of political, economic, and geographic contexts

Originally published on Global Voices

Image by Gerd Altmann on Pixabay.

Fifteen years ago I wrote an article about “networked authoritarianism,” describing China as “exhibit A” for how an authoritarian state adapts to the internet and then adapts digital technologies to increase its own power. I sought to counter prevailing narratives of the time that the internet and tech companies were intrinsically a liberating, democratizing force. While such narratives were eventually discredited, we must not give up on our ability to use technology to defend and exercise our rights. Nor can we simply demand that governments and companies solve the problems they jointly continue to create.

October’s spotlight on Big Tech and Authoritarianism explored a range of relationships between tech companies and political actors across the global majority. Power is wielded through digital technologies in many ways. There are no quick fixes or easy solutions to stop abuses.

title: Save Our Stories: Why Libraries Need the Law on Their Side
content:
Today, 5 November, is World Digital Preservation Day, and this year’s theme, “Save our Stories (SOS): Our digital heritage in danger”, could not be more timely for libraries.

Few missions are more central to libraries than preservation. From local history collections in public libraries to rare books in academic centres and the full national bibliographies held by national libraries, ensuring that the past and present survive into the future is a core role.

Preservation, crucially, is less about an attachment to the past than about an investment in the future. Without it, researchers, communities, and citizens are all the poorer. Access to facts, records and ideas is vital for study, democratic transparency, and the fulfilment of cultural rights.

There are therefore plenty of reasons to be concerned about a 21st-century black hole in library collections that is only getting deeper.

title: Hunajaa valtion vihollisen kanssa
content:
Ajoimme nelivetoisella jeepillä läpi Tigrayn vuoristoa. Vuosi oli 2021, ja sota pohjoisessa Etiopiassa oli raivonnut jo yli puoli vuotta. Pysähdyimme pieneen kylään, ja ympärillä alkoi vilkas keskustelu ja kova kuhina. Olin sanonut, että olisi kiinnostavaa päästä haastattelemaan paikallisten kapinallisten sotilaita heidän ajatuksistaan.
Se kyllä järjestyisi, ja järjestyipä toinenkin haastattelu.

Yhtäkkiä istuin savitalossa jakkaralla pienen pöydän äärellä. Pöydällä oli purkki tuoretta hunajaa ja jokaiselle lusikka. Vastapäätä istui ­Getachew Reda, Etiopian entinen viestintäministeri ja silloinen kapinallisjohtaja. Hän oli hallituksen halutuimpia henkilöitä, elävänä tai kuolleena. Mieluiten kuolleena.

Emme me häntä tietenkään sattumalta löytäneet, vaan hän halusi tulla löydetyksi ja kertoa asiansa. Myös muutama muu kollega oli pääsyt hänen juttusilleen, mutta esimerkiksi ruotsalainen kilpailijani sairastui koronaan eikä päässyt lähtemään maasta. Voitin uutiskilpailun.

title: Culture is back on the Horizon – Parliament compromise text
content:
The Name Place Fund coalition, which brings together culture and research organisations advocating for stronger support for culture in Horizon Europe and the European Competitiveness Fund, welcomes the cross-party compromise text on Horizon Europe 2028-2034 negotiated in the European Parliament. 

The compromise text was prepared by rapporteurs Christian Ehler (EPP) and René Repasi (S&D) together with the shadow rapporteurs. The compromise is scheduled for a vote in Parliament’s Industry, Research and Energy (ITRE) Committee on 10 November. This text will be the starting point for the Parliament’s negotiations with the Commission and the Council. 

After long negotiations, culture, creativity and artistic research finally have a more prominent place in the future EU research and innovation programme, signalling an important shift in how the role of arts and culture in research and innovation is understood.

We covered a recap of what happened in the last months in this article.

title: Using personalisation makes every AI chat less risky and more effective — here are five essential custom instructions to add
content:
One of best things you can do to lower the risks of using AI and improve the quality of outputs is to spend five minutes with one of AI tools’ least-used features: their personalisation settings.

ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Claude all have personalisation features: a section of the tool where you can give it permanent extra information that informs every conversation. You can find it in your general settings under names like ‘instructions’, ‘personal context’ or ‘personalization’, or using the links above.

Here are five instructions you can include in that section:

Your professional role, ethics, location, language, skill level and other details all provide vital context that will help reduce assumptions and misunderstandings and improve the ‘predictions’ that AI tools make when responding.

title: Pedaalin uusi kuvatukikorttipakka kokeiluvaiheeseen
content:
Pedaalin jäsenistöstä koottu kuvatukikorttityöryhmä ja graafikko Mari Kasurinen ovat saaneet valmiiksi ensimmäisen testiversion Pedaalin kuvatukikorttipakasta. Pedaali jakaa testiversiota Tien päällä-kiertueellaan vuodenvaihteen molemmin puolin ja myös Lahden osallisuusseminaarin yhteydessä pakkaan pääsee tutustumaan.

Korttipakan testiversion käyttöön ottaneilta edellytetään palautetta pakasta. Pedaali pyytää palautetta korttipakasta ja sen käytettävyydestä kevään 2027 aikana, jotta korttipakasta saadaan kehitettyä mahdollisimman monia museoita hyödyttävä osallisuuden apuväline.

title: Kulttuuriala vetoaa Yleen: Puku- ja rekvisiittavarastoille on löydettävä jatkoa
content:
Sunklo on allekirjoittanut vetoomuksen YLE:lle yhdessä muiden kulttuurialan järjestöjen kanssa puku- ja rekvisiittavarastojen säilyttämiseksi.

Elokuva-, televisio-, teatteri-, tanssi- ja sirkusalan järjestöt sekä yli 100 alan ammattilaista vaativat avoimessa kirjeessä, että Yleisradio keskeyttää puku-, rekvisiitta- ja lavastevarastojensa esineistön hävittämisen. Hävittäminen on keskeytettävä siihen asti, kunnes kokoelmien tuleva sijoituspaikka ja vuokraustoiminnan jatkuminen on selvitetty.

Yle on ilmoittanut tavoitteekseen ajaa vuokraustoimintansa alas. Vuosikymmenten aikana verovaroin kartutettua kokoelmaa käyttävät Ylen omien tuotantojen lisäksi kaupalliset tuotantoyhtiöt ja freelancerit eri puolilla kotimaista av-alaa. Kokoelman menettäminen vaarantaisi erityisesti historiallisten elokuvien ja sarjojen tekemisen Suomessa ja moninkertaistaisi tuotantojen hankintakulut ja tekijöiden työkuorman. Lisäksi se purkaisi toimivan kiertotalousmallin juuri silloin, kun alalta edellytetään entistä vastuullisempia toimintatapoja.

title: What the US midterms result means for the Ukraine war
content:
The US midterm elections have shifted the balance of power in Congress, delivering a massive blow to Donald Trump and his Republican party. This has implications both at home and possibly abroad, including for US policy towards Ukraine; an issue that was hardly mentioned during the campaigns.

But even if Ukraine did not figure much in the election, the question in US politics of what to do about the war has not gone away. Indeed, in the weeks and months before the result was announced, Trump had been busily rowing back on US support for Ukraine. This was despite much opposition, even from some Republicans.

Crucial intelligence to Kyiv about Russian strikes was cut off, before later being reinstated, while critical military aid was reduced. Trump also decided to suspend several sanctions on Russia.

This move was denounced by President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine as only helping Russia, but justified by Trump as being “in the national interests of the United States” and also a decision that might help his party’s electoral chances by reducing gas prices.

title: Why AI cannot ‘think’ like humans do
content:
Today’s artificial intelligence technologies have become remarkably good at generating text and ideas that seem profoundly human. Chatbots powered by large language models such as ChatGPT, Claude, Google Gemini and Perplexity AI can write poems, brainstorm and find solutions to complex problems.

The developers of these products drew heavily on the human brain for inspiration, creating artificial neural networks based on the workings of human neurons. Their systems now produce outputs that often resemble the outputs of human thinking.

AI and the human mind, however, do not work the same way. Similar results do not necessarily mean similar processes.

“World models” are an emerging technology that could help AI systems move closer to human “thinking” by helping them learn to anticipate what might happen and use that prediction to act. Still, AI will not perceive, learn or understand the world as humanity does.

Imagine reaching for a cup at the edge of a counter. The cup may fall and smash if you misjudge the distance, grip it too loosely or move too quickly.

A monthly gift gives us something particularly valuable: the confidence to plan ahead. To maintain the unglamorous-but-essential infrastructure, respond when democracy changes, and build the next thing people need — without putting our core services behind a paywall or plastering them with advertising.

A monthly donation is a wonderfully simple way to help make sure those tools are still accessible the next time somebody needs them.

title: WiNoDa Conference 2026 “Beyond drawers and spreadsheets: the journey of object-related data” – a lively community event
content:
With participants in the conference room of the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin and numerous people joining online, at 9:30 in the morning of October 21, 2026, we declared the conference “Beyond drawers and spreadsheets: the journey of object-related data” officially open.

We kicked off the conference with an introduction from our coordinator, Cora Albrecht, who warmly welcomed participants and then briefly introduced WiNoDa and some of its milestones from the last two years.

Then Mareike Petersen, head of the Science Programme “Collection Future” at MfN, nicely framed the day’s topic, highlighting how much data can be extracted from collections of natural objects while also noting some of the most common challenges in working with historical information. WiNoDa’s learning offers aim to lower the access barrier to this data, making it useful for researchers and museum staff around the world.

After the introductory talk, it was time for our community. We received numerous excellent submissions for the conference from the following subject areas:

  • Collection management and standardisation
  • Data reuse for research and conservation
  • Digitisation workflows
  • AI and computational methods

title: Everyone Everywhere Hated Meta’s New AI Training Terms. Now, They’re On Pause
content:
Following widespread backlash, Meta announced earlier this week it’s putting a planned update of its commercial terms of use on pause. The terms would have required business accounts to allow Meta to “use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of” Meta’s products. 

The new terms were initially set to go into effect on October 30, but after outcry from journalists and users who didn’t want Meta reaching far beyond Instagram and Facebook and into their websites to suck up their work as training data for its generative AI products, Meta announced it was pushing the change to November 20. Now, it’s on hold entirely. 

“We recently shared that we were updating the Meta Commercial Terms, Product Catalog Terms, Self-Serve Ad Terms, and Ad Creative Generative AI Terms,” Meta says on the page where the commercial terms announcement used to be. “These updates are now paused and will not take effect on November 20, 2026. We are continuing to consult with stakeholders and will provide a further update when we have more to share. In the meantime, our existing terms remain in effect.”

title: Israel/OPT: Israel must immediately release Palestinian farmer and land defender Ghassan Najjar
content:
In response to the Israeli military’s arrest of Palestinian farmer and land defender Ghassan Najjar during a pre-dawn raid on the village of Burin south of Nablus in the northern occupied West Bank, on 27 October, Erika Guevara Rosas, Amnesty International’s Senior Director for Research, Policy, Advocacy and Campaigns, said:

“Israeli authorities must immediately release Ghassan Najjar who was arrested solely because of his peaceful activism to protect the olive harvest season in Burin. Israeli intelligence agents had explicitly threatened Ghassan Najjar, co-founder of Burin’s Land and Farming Agricultural Cooperative, that he would be arrested if he did not stop his activism. His activism includes community organizing, supporting mutual aid among farmers through the cooperative, organizing an annual Kite Festival in the village and leading numerous cultural initiatives. Ghassan Najjar had been facing repeated threats since the start of the olive harvest season and their frequency intensified during the week prior to his arrest.

title: How Online Maps Lay Bare the US Military Bases Targeted by Iran
content:

In September, CBS News obtained new images of the aftermath of attacks on US bases in the Middle East from active service members. One told the news channel: “This is major damage to our bases that hasn’t been communicated to the American public. “We’re standing there with our eyes closed getting punched in the face,” they added.

While reports have detailed how Iran used Russian intelligence, including satellite imagery, to identify US troops, ships and aircraft, Bellingcat found that publicly available mapping platforms also reveal detailed and potentially sensitive information about US military bases in the Middle East. 

Google Maps and other online mapping services contain dozens of labels identifying facilities including headquarters, accommodation, gyms and fuel points. Publicly available photographs and videos, including material published by the US military, provide further details about how these facilities are used.

title: Interactive: Tracking negotiating texts at the COP31 climate summit
content:
The centrepiece of every UN climate summit is for countries to negotiate the wording of a large number of legal agreements – and COP31 in the Turkish city of Antalya is no different.

These texts are hashed out behind closed doors in the “blue zone” at the COP, where diplomats from nearly 200 nations – not including the US – will be haggling over each individual verb.

Over the course of the two-week summit, negotiators will be trying to reach consensus on more than 100 separate agreements – but, first, they must agree which issues are on the agenda.

The complexity of this process can make it challenging to keep track of what countries are fighting about and how negotiations are progressing.

Carbon Brief’s real-time text tracker, below, offers a helping hand by decoding the agenda and keeping a searchable record of every document for each part of the negotiations.

The first column of the interactive tracker lists the topic of each agenda item, with further columns including dates, page counts and links to the original PDFs.

The table is searchable via the interactive text box and can be sorted using the arrow icons.
